10.1016/j.media.2026.104079.title: Future cardiovascular events prediction from invasive coronary angiography: A graph representation learning perspective
10.1016/j.media.2026.104079.abstract: Improving risk stratification for coronary artery disease (CAD), the leading global cause of death, remains a daily challenge in clinical practice. This highlights the urgent need for innovative approaches to early prediction of future cardiovascular events from invasive coronary angiography (ICA), the gold standard imaging modality for CAD diagnosis. However, current methods, including clinical indices and data-driven deep learning models, fail to tackle this challenge. In this work, we propose AngioGraphCAD, a graph neural network-based framework for patient-level future cardiovascular events prediction from ICA. By design, the framework flexibly accommodates the variable number of coronary lesions per patient, enabling robust patient-level prediction. For each lesion, AngioGraphCAD constructs a geometric graph representation and learns a lesion-level embedding that leverages coronary artery geometry alongside clinical data, together with a lesion-level prediction objective. These lesion-level embeddings are then fused using a novel masked-attention mechanism to form a unified and interpretable patient-level representation. Across two clinical cohorts (FAME2: 563 patients, 1551 stenoses; FCL: 83 patients, 382 stenoses), AngioGraphCAD achieves strong lesion-level performance, significantly outperforming clinical measures and CNN-based models, with AUCs of 0.71 (FAME2) and 0.73 (FCL). Building on these lesion-level representations, AngioGraphCAD further achieves an AUC of 0.70 for patient-level prediction on FAME2. Overall, this study underscores the predictive value of coronary artery geometry from ICA and highlights geometry-aware representations as a promising step toward more personalized CAD management.

10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2026.03.009.title: From canopy to ground via ForestGen3D: Learning cross-domain generation of 3D forest structure from aerial-to-terrestrial LiDAR
10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2026.03.009.abstract: The 3D structure of living and non-living components in ecosystems plays a critical role in determining ecological processes and feedbacks from both natural and human-driven disturbances. Anticipating the effects of wildfire, drought, disease, or atmospheric deposition depends on accurate characterization of 3D vegetation structure, yet widespread measurement remains prohibitively expensive and often infeasible. We present ForestGen3D, a cross-domain generative framework that preserves ALS observed 3D forest structure while inferring missing sub-canopy detail. ForestGen3D is based on conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic models trained on co-registered ALS and terrestrial LiDAR (TLS) data, exploiting the empirical containment of TLS structure within the ALS derived spatial envelope. The model generates realistic TLS-like point clouds that remain spatially consistent with ALS geometry while smoothly reconstructing canopy interior, mid-story, and near-ground structure, enabling landscape-scalable reconstruction of full vertical forest structure. To ensure ecological plausibility, we introduce a geometric containment prior based on the convex hull of ALS observations and provide theoretical and empirical guarantees that generated structures remain spatially consistent. We evaluate ForestGen3D at tree, plot, and landscape scales using real-world data from mixed conifer ecosystems, and show through qualitative and quantitative geometric and distributional analyses that it produces high-fidelity reconstructions closely matching TLS reference data in terms of 3D structural similarity and downstream biophysical metrics, including tree height, DBH, crown diameter, and crown volume. We further demonstrate that the resulting expected point containment (EPC) serves as a practical proxy for generation quality in settings where TLS ground truth is unavailable. Our results demonstrate that ForestGen3D enhances the utility of ALS only environments by inferring ecologically plausible sub-canopy structure while faithfully preserving the landscape heterogeneity encoded in ALS observations, thereby providing a richer 3D representation for ecological analysis, structural fuel characterization and related remote sensing applications.

10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2025.12.023.title: A Spatially Masked Adaptive Gated Network for multimodal post-flood water extent mapping using SAR and incomplete multispectral data
10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2025.12.023.abstract: Mapping water extent during a flood event is essential for effective disaster management throughout all phases: mitigation, preparedness, response, and recovery. In particular, during the response stage, when timely and accurate information is important, Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data are primarily employed to produce water extent maps. This is because SAR sensors can observe through cloud cover and operate both day and night, whereas Multispectral Imaging (MSI) data, despite providing higher mapping accuracy, are only available under cloud-free and daytime conditions. Recently, leveraging the complementary characteristics of SAR and MSI data through a multimodal approach has emerged as a promising strategy for advancing water extent mapping using deep learning models. This approach is particularly beneficial when timely post-flood observations, acquired during or shortly after the flood peak, are limited, as it enables the use of all available imagery for more accurate post-flood water extent mapping. However, the adaptive integration of partially available MSI data into the SAR-based post-flood water extent mapping process remains underexplored. To bridge this research gap, we propose the Spatially Masked Adaptive Gated Network (SMAGNet), a multimodal deep learning model that utilizes SAR data as the primary input for post-flood water extent mapping and integrates complementary MSI data through feature fusion. In experiments on the C2S-MS Floods dataset, SMAGNet consistently outperformed other multimodal deep learning models in prediction performance across varying levels of MSI data availability. Specifically, SMAGNet achieved the highest IoU score of 86.47% using SAR and MSI data and maintained the highest performance with an IoU score of 79.53% even when MSI data were entirely missing. Furthermore, we found that even when MSI data were completely missing, the performance of SMAGNet remained statistically comparable to that of a U-Net model trained solely on SAR data. These findings indicate that SMAGNet enhances the model robustness to missing data as well as the applicability of multimodal deep learning in real-world flood management scenarios. The source code is available at https://github.com/ASUcicilab/SMAGNet.

10.1016/j.cemconcomp.2025.106436.title: Natural carbonation of concrete: a data-driven analysis
10.1016/j.cemconcomp.2025.106436.abstract: This study presents a data-driven analysis of long-term natural carbonation in concrete, using a newly compiled database comprising 1079 mixes and 8194 carbonation depth measurements over 65 years, representing one of the largest natural carbonation datasets assembled to date. Four different tree-based machine learning models (CatBoost, XGBoost, Random Forest and Decision Tree) were evaluated for predicting carbonation rate (k), with CatBoost emerging as the most effective. Partial dependence and SHAP analyses were used to quantify the relative importance of 13 features influencing k, including binder composition, mix proportion, curing and exposure conditions. The water-to-calcium oxide (w/CaO) ratio emerges as the most important feature, encapsulating the effects of porosity, carbonatable content, and supplementary cementitious material (SCM) type and content. Higher SCM replacement levels increase carbonation, while aggregate-related features show comparatively less pronounced effects. Carbonation environment is a more important feature than curing condition in predicting k. By combining machine learning with interpretable SHAP analysis, the model independently recognised trends consistent with literature findings. This study offers a comprehensive dataset and robustly selected features to facilitate future machine learning-based predictions of concrete carbonation.

10.1016/j.medj.2026.101176.title: The atlas of abdominal organ remodeling in hepatocellular carcinoma patients: An artificial intelligence-based multicenter imaging study
10.1016/j.medj.2026.101176.abstract: Summary Background Morphological changes of abdominal organs in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain uncharacterized. This study aimed to automatically quantify these changes using deep learning, assess their treatment-related outcome associations, and evaluate prognostic value. Methods Abdominal computed tomography (CT) images from 2,747 patients with HCC and 2,869 healthy controls across 15 cohorts from 10 centers (8 Chinese and 2 international) were analyzed. The patients included those receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), or surgical resection. A deep learning algorithm automatically segmented the spleen, liver, kidneys, pancreas, and adrenal glands. Organ volumes and height-normalized indexes (volume/height2) were calculated. Propensity score matching balanced baseline differences. Cox regression assessed associations with overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), and disease-free survival (DFS), with subgroup and interaction analyses. Findings Compared with healthy controls, patients with HCC showed significant organ remodeling, with enlarged spleen, liver, kidneys, and adrenal glands (all p < 0.001). Multivariable analysis showed that in the ICI cohort, left kidney volume/index, right kidney index, and left adrenal gland volume/index predicted longer OS and PFS; in the TACE cohort, spleen volume/index and left kidney volume predicted OS and PFS; and in the surgical cohort, spleen volume, left kidney volume, left adrenal gland volume/index, and liver index were independent predictors. Restricted cubic spline analysis suggested nonlinear relationships between adrenal and kidney volumes and survival. Conclusions HCC is associated with systemic abdominal organ remodeling. Automated CT-based multi-organ quantification offers reproducible, non-invasive prognostic biomarkers, particularly in cases involving adrenal glands, spleen, and kidneys, supporting personalized treatment and prognosis assessment. 10.1016/j.jmsy.2025.12.019.title: Safe reinforcement learning with online filtering for fatigue-predictive human–robot task planning and allocation in production
10.1016/j.jmsy.2025.12.019.abstract: Human–robot collaborative manufacturing, a core aspect of Industry 5.0, emphasizes ergonomics to enhance worker well-being. This paper addresses the dynamic human–robot task planning and allocation (HRTPA) problem, which involves determining when to perform tasks and who should execute them to maximize efficiency while ensuring workers’ physical fatigue remains within safe limits. The inclusion of fatigue constraints, combined with production dynamics, significantly increases the complexity of the HRTPA problem. Traditional fatigue–recovery models in HRTPA often rely on static, predefined hyperparameters. However, in practice, human fatigue sensitivity varies daily due to factors such as changed work conditions and insufficient sleep. To better capture this uncertainty, we treat fatigue-related parameters as inaccurate and estimate them online based on observed fatigue progression during production. To address these challenges, we propose PF-CD3Q, a safe reinforcement learning (safe RL) approach that integrates the particle filter with constrained dueling double deep Q-learning for real-time fatigue-predictive HRTPA. Specifically, we first develop PF-based estimators to track human fatigue and update fatigue model parameters in real-time. These estimators are then integrated into CD3Q by making task-level fatigue predictions during decision-making and excluding tasks that exceed fatigue limits, thereby constraining the action space and formulating the problem as a constrained Markov decision process (CMDP). Experimental results demonstrate that our PF-based estimators achieve high prediction accuracy and strong noise robustness, and that PF-CD3Q outperforms other algorithms across multiple performance metrics, significantly reducing the occurrence of overwork and adapting to unseen fatigue constraints after training. These findings validate the effectiveness of our approach under complex and dynamic production conditions, supporting both human well-being and the development of a more sustainable and efficient manufacturing paradigm.

10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2026.02.024.title: SpecAware: a spectral-content aware foundation model for unifying multi-sensor learning in hyperspectral remote sensing mapping
10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2026.02.024.abstract: Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) is a critical technique for fine-grained land-use and land-cover (LULC) mapping. However, the inherent heterogeneity of HSI data, particularly the variation in spectral channels across sensors, has long constrained the development of model generalization via transfer learning or joint training. Existing HSI foundation models show promise for different downstream tasks, but typically underutilize the critical guiding role of sensor meta-attributes and image semantic features, resulting in limited adaptability to cross-sensor joint learning. To address these issues, we propose SpecAware, which is a novel hyperspectral spectral-content aware foundation model for unifying multi-sensor learning for HSI mapping. To support this work, we constructed the Hyper-400K dataset, which is a new large-scale pre-training dataset with over 400 k high-quality patches from diverse airborne AVIRIS sensors that cover two data processing levels (L1 and L2). The core of SpecAware is a hypernetwork-driven unified image embedding process for HSI data. Firstly, we designed a meta-content aware module to generate a unique conditional input for each HSI sample, tailored to each spectral band by fusing the sensor meta-attributes and its own image content. Secondly, we designed the HyperEmbedding module, where a sample-conditioned hypernetwork dynamically generates a pair of matrix factors for channel-wise encoding. This process implements two-step matrix factorization, consisting of adaptive spatial pattern extraction and latent semantic feature projection, yielding a unified hyperspectral token representation. Thus, SpecAware learns to capture and interpret spatial-spectral features across diverse scenes and sensors, enabling adaptive processing of variable spectral channels within a unified multi-sensor joint pre-training framework. Extensive experiments on seven datasets demonstrate that SpecAware can learn competitive feature representations, compared to the existing pre-trained models, achieving superior performance in a suite of LULC tasks, including large-scale land-cover semantic segmentation, change detection, and scene classification. The proposed SpecAware model will be released at https://github.com/busbyjrj/SpecAware.

10.1016/s2352-4642(25)00314-1.title: Diagnostic labels and clusters based on oxygen requirements in preterm infants with chronic lung disease: a data-driven exploratory cluster analysis in two independent cohorts
10.1016/s2352-4642(25)00314-1.abstract: Summary Background Diagnosis of bronchopulmonary dysplasia in very low birthweight infants is often only ascertained many weeks after birth. We aimed to investigate whether trajectories of the fractions of inspired oxygen (FiO2) required to maintain O2 saturation from birth reflect distinct clusters of preterm lung disease. Methods In this data-driven exploratory cluster analysis, we used latent class trajectory modelling to derive clusters of FiO2 fluctuations in the first 30 days of life among neonates with a birthweight of less than 1250 g, across two multicentre, prospective cohorts: the Discovery Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia Program (D-BPD; enrolment July 30, 2013, to Jan 1, 2020; n=376) in Argentina and the Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP; enrolment Aug 1, 2011, to Nov 31, 2013; n=835) in the USA, with the PROP cohort being used for external validation. Eligible participants, in both the present and original studies, included infants with birthweight of less than 1250 g in the D-BPD cohort, and infants enrolled in the PROP study born at 23–28 weeks of gestation by best obstetrical estimate. After unsupervised clustering of patients, we evaluated cluster performance against conventional bronchopulmonary dysplasia classification, using mortality as the primary outcome. Findings Of the 376 D-BPD infants, 190 (51%) were female (mean birthweight 968·1 g [SD 181·2]; mean gestational age 28·9 weeks [SD 2·3]) and 186 (49%) were male (mean birthweight 976·2 g [188·3]; mean gestational age 28·6 weeks [2·3]). Four clusters based on FiO2 requirements were identified: persistently low requirement (PLR; 218 [58%] of 376), early high with subsequent improvement (EHRI; 60 [16%] of 376), late-onset high requirement (LOHR; 31 [8%] of 376), and persistently high requirement (PHR; 67 [18%] of 376). Mortality was more frequent in LOHR (six [19%] of 31) and PHR (ten [15%] of 67) clusters, with no deaths in PLR and one death in EHRI (one [2%] of 60; p<0·0001). Nine (53%) of 17 fatal cases occurred before 36 weeks' gestational age, precluding conventional bronchopulmonary dysplasia diagnosis; among infants who died later, most had severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia (six [67%] of nine). Results from the PROP cohort closely mirrored those of D-BPD, yielding the same number of clusters with similar trajectories and replicating patterns of mortality. Interpretation Current bronchopulmonary dysplasia definitions might not fully capture the trajectories of lung disease of preterm infants. Data-driven approaches offer opportunities to identify infants at high risk earlier and to implement more precise interventions. 10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2026.01.023.title: SuperMapNet for long-range and high-accuracy vectorized HD map construction
10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2026.01.023.abstract: Vectorized high-definition (HD) map construction is formulated as the task of classifying and localizing typical map elements based on features in a bird’s-eye view (BEV). This is essential for autonomous driving systems, providing interpretable environmental structured representations for decision and planning. Remarkable work has been achieved in recent years, but several major issues remain: (1) in the generation of the BEV features, single modality methods suffer from limited perception capability and range, while existing multi-modal fusion approaches underutilize cross-modal synergies and fail to resolve spatial disparities between modalities, resulting in misaligned BEV features with holes; (2) in the classification and localization of map elements, existing methods heavily rely on point-level modeling information while neglecting the information between elements and between point and element, leading to low accuracy with erroneous shapes and element entanglement. To address these limitations, we propose SuperMapNet, a multi-modal framework designed for long-range and high-accuracy vectorized HD map construction. This framework uses both camera images and LiDAR point clouds as input. It first tightly couples semantic information from camera images and geometric information from LiDAR point clouds by a cross-attention based synergy enhancement module and a flow-based disparity alignment module for long-range BEV feature generation. Subsequently, local information acquired by point queries and global information acquired by element queries are tightly coupled by three-level interactions for high-accuracy classification and localization, where Point2Point interaction captures local geometric consistency between points of the same element, Element2Element interaction learns global semantic relationships between elements, and Point2Element interaction complement element information for its constituent points. Experiments on the nuScenes and Argoverse2 datasets demonstrate high accuracy, surpassing previous state-of-the-art methods (SOTAs) by 14.9%/8.8% and 18.5%/3.1% mAP under the hard/easy settings, respectively, even over the double perception ranges (up to 120 m in the X-axis and 60 m in the Y-axis). The code is made publicly available at https://github.com/zhouruqin/SuperMapNet.

10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2025.12.004.title: Enhancing monocular height estimation via sparse LiDAR-guided correction
10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2025.12.004.abstract: Monocular height estimation (MHE) from very-high-resolution (VHR) remote sensing imagery via deep learning is notoriously challenging due to the lack of sufficient structural information. Conventional digital elevation models (DEMs), typically derived from airborne LiDAR or multi-view stereo, remain costly and geographically limited. While state-of-the-art monocular height estimation (MHE) and depth estimation (MDE) models show great promise, their robustness under varied illumination conditions remains a significant challenge. To address this, we introduce a novel and fully automated correction pipeline that integrates sparse, imperfect global LiDAR measurements (ICESat-2) with deep learning outputs to enhance local accuracy and robustness. Importantly, the entire workflow is fully automated and built solely on publicly available models and datasets, requiring only a single georeferenced optical image to generate corrected height maps, thereby ensuring unprecedented accessibility and global scalability. Furthermore, we establish the first comprehensive benchmark for this task, evaluating a suite of correction methods that includes two random forest-based approaches, four parameter-efficient fine-tuning techniques, and full fine-tuning. We conduct extensive experiments across six large-scale, diverse regions at 0.5m resolution, totaling approximately 297km2, encompassing the urban cores of Tokyo, Paris, and São Paulo, as well as mixed suburban and forest landscapes. Experimental results demonstrate that the best-performing correction method reduces the MHE model’s mean absolute error (MAE) by an average of 30.9% and improves its F1HE score by 44.2%. For the MDE model, the MAE is improved by 24.1% and the F1HE score by 25.1%. These findings validate the effectiveness of our correction pipeline, demonstrating how sparse real-world LiDAR data can systematically bolster the robustness of both MHE and MDE models and paving the way for scalable, low-cost, and globally applicable 3D mapping solutions.

10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2026.06.008.title: SpectralX: Parameter-efficient domain generalization for spectral Remote Sensing Foundation Models
10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2026.06.008.abstract: Recent advances in Remote Sensing Foundation Models (RSFMs) have led to significant breakthroughs in the field. While many RSFMs have been pretrained with massive optical imagery, more multispectral/hyperspectral data remain lack of the corresponding foundation models. To leverage the advantages of spectral imagery in earth observation, we explore whether existing RSFMs can be effectively adapted to process diverse spectral modalities without requiring extensive spectral pretraining. In response to this challenge, we proposed SpectralX, an innovative parameter-efficient fine-tuning framework that adapt existing RSFMs as backbone while introducing a two-stage training approach to handle various spectral inputs, thereby significantly improving domain generalization performance. In the first stage, we employ a masked-reconstruction task and design a specialized Hyper Tokenizer (HyperT) to extract attribute tokens from both spatial and spectral dimensions. Simultaneously, we develop an Attribute-oriented Mixture of Adapter (AoMoA) that dynamically modulate features while performing layer-wise fine-tuning. With semantic segmentation as downstream task in the second stage, we plug an Attribute-refined Adapter (Are-adapter) behind AoMoA. By iteratively querying low-level semantic features with high-level representations, the model learns to focus on task-beneficial features, enabling customized adjustment of RSFMs. Following this two-phase adaptation process, SpectralX is capable of interpreting spectral imagery from new regions or seasons. We have collected three benchmark spectral datasets and constructed eight domain generalization tasks. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that SpectralX effectively adapts to diverse spectral imagery and outperforms state-of-the-art methods in cross-domain interpretation tasks. SpectralX achieves average improvements of 4.2% mIoU and 3.5% mIoU over RSFMs under without and with domain-gap settings, respectively. The codes will be available from the website: https://github.com/YuxiangZhang-BIT/SpectralX.

10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2026.08.027.title: AWARE: Adaptive whole-body active rotating control for enhanced LiDAR-inertial odometry under human-in-the-loop interaction
10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2026.08.027.abstract: Human-in-the-loop (HITL) UAV operation is essential in complex and safety-critical aerial surveying environments, where human operators provide navigation intent while onboard autonomy must maintain accurate and robust state estimation. A key challenge in this setting is that resource-constrained UAV platforms are often limited to narrow-field-of-view LiDAR sensors. In geometrically degenerate or feature-sparse scenes, limited sensing coverage often weakens LiDAR Inertial Odometry (LIO)’s observability, causing drift accumulation, degraded geometric accuracy, and unstable state estimation, which directly compromise safe and effective HITL operation and the reliability of downstream surveying products. To overcome this limitation, we present AWARE, a bio-inspired whole-body active yawing framework that exploits the UAV’s own rotational agility to extend the effective sensor horizon and improve LIO’s observability without additional mechanical actuation. The core of AWARE is a differentiable Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework embedded in a Reinforcement Learning (RL) loop. It first identifies the viewing direction that maximizes information gain across the full yaw space, and a lightweight RL agent then adjusts the MPC cost weights online according to the current environmental context, enabling an adaptive balance between estimation accuracy and flight stability. A Safe Flight Corridor mechanism further ensures operational safety within this HITL paradigm by decoupling the operator’s navigational intent from autonomous yaw optimization to enable safe and efficient cooperative control. We validate AWARE through extensive experiments in diverse simulated and real-world environments. 10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2026.09.002.title: A mechanism-coupled split-window network for medium- to high-resolution land surface temperature retrieval
10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2026.09.002.abstract: Land surface temperature (LST) retrieval from medium- to high-resolution thermal infrared (TIR) observations remains challenging under complex atmospheric and surface conditions. Traditional split window (SW) algorithms rely on empirical coefficients whose adaptability may be limited under complex scenarios such as high temperature and high humidity, whereas purely data-driven models often lack explicit physical constraints and may generalize poorly beyond the training distribution. To address these issues, this study proposes a Parallel Component Decoupled Neural Network (PCD-Net) that reformulates SW retrieval as an adaptive learning problem of physical component parameters. Using the SW equation as the physical backbone, PCD-Net decomposes the retrieval process into constant, first-order, and second-order brightness temperature difference terms; meanwhile, a residual branch is incorporated to supplement the nonlinear coupling corrections induced by the joint effects of surface emissivity and atmospheric water vapor. Parallel subnetworks dynamically estimate the corresponding coefficients from atmospheric water vapor and land surface emissivity. PCD-Net is first initialized and jointly optimized using MODTRAN-based radiative transfer simulations and is subsequently fine-tuned with in situ LST observations to reduce deviation between simulated and real observational conditions. Validation using 4,450 Landsat–in situ samples from 29 globally distributed benchmark sites shows that PCD-Net achieves a mean absolute error (MAE) of 1.84 K, a root mean square error (RMSE) of 2.55 K, and a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.966, outperforming the traditional split window mechanistic model (MM(SW)), the radiative transfer mechanistic model (MM(RT)), and the ML baseline. Under extremely low or high LST and atmospheric water vapor conditions, PCD-Net substantially reduces retrieval errors relative to the traditional MM(SW), with reductions exceeding 50% in some scenarios. Sensitivity analysis further indicates that PCD-Net exhibits smoother responses to perturbations in at-sensor radiance, atmospheric water vapor content, and land surface emissivity.

10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2025.11.017.title: TasselNetV4: A vision foundation model for cross-scene, cross-scale, and cross-species plant counting
10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2025.11.017.abstract: Accurate plant counting provides valuable information for agriculture such as crop yield prediction, plant density assessment, and phenotype quantification. Vision-based approaches are currently the mainstream solution. Prior art typically uses a detection or a regression model to count a specific plant. However, plants have biodiversity, and new cultivars are increasingly bred each year. It is almost impossible to exhaust and build all species-dependent counting models. Inspired by class-agnostic counting (CAC) in computer vision, we argue that it is time to rethink the problem formulation of plant counting, from what plants to count to how to count plants. In contrast to most daily objects with spatial and temporal invariance, plants are dynamic, changing with time and space. Their non-rigid structure often leads to worse performance than counting rigid instances like heads and cars such that current CAC and open-world detection models are suboptimal to count plants. In this work, we inherit the vein of the TasselNet plant counting model and introduce a new extension, TasselNetV4, shifting from species-specific counting to cross-species counting. TasselNetV4 marries the local counting idea of TasselNet with the extract-and-match paradigm in CAC. It builds upon a plain vision transformer and incorporates novel multi-branch box-aware local counters used to enhance cross-scale robustness. In particular, two challenging datasets, PAC-105 and PAC-Somalia, are harvested. PAC-105 features 105 plant- and organ-level categories from 64 plant species, spanning various scenes. PAC-Somalia, specific to out-of-distribution validation, features 32 unique plant species in Somalia. Extensive experiments against state-of-the-art CAC models show that TasselNetV4 achieves not only superior counting performance but also high efficiency, with a mean absolute error of 16.04, an R2 of 0.92, and up to 121 FPS inference speed on images of 384 × 384 resolution. Our results indicate that TasselNetV4 emerges to be a vision foundation model for cross-scene, cross-scale, and cross-species plant counting. To facilitate future plant counting research, we plan to release all the data, annotations, code, and pretrained models at https://github.com/tiny-smart/tasselnetv4.

10.1016/j.ress.2026.113708.title: Mining of fault propagation mechanisms in computer numerical control machine tools via information fusion and association rules
10.1016/j.ress.2026.113708.abstract: Enhancing the reliability of CNC (Computer Numerical Control) machine tools requires precise identification of fault propagation paths. However, existing methods often treat macroscopic topology and microscopic mechanisms in isolation and suffer from biases inherent in single-source data. To address these issues, this paper proposes a reliability-oriented mechanism mining framework integrating information fusion and Association Rule Mining (ARM). First, a game-theoretic weighted Decision Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL)–Interpretive Structural Modeling (ISM) method is proposed to fuse expert knowledge with failure statistics. This constructs a robust hierarchical topology that mitigates data sparsity. Second, using this topology as a physical constraint, a constraint-based Apriori algorithm is developed. With downtime-centric constraints, it extracts microscopic failure mechanisms from abstract paths. It also overcomes the limitations of traditional algorithms in capturing temporal logic and fault chains. A case study on a five-axis machining center identifies the Electrical System as the most influential subsystem within the identified fault propagation topology and the Automatic Tool Changer (ATC) as the most susceptible unit. The proposed method detects latent High-Impact Low-Probability (HILP) chains and improves Precision, Recall, and F1-score by 2.56 ×, 1.75 ×, and 2.16 × over the traditional algorithm. These results demonstrate improved consistency with the topology-constrained reference patterns for reliability diagnosis of complex electromechanical systems.

10.1016/j.ress.2026.113592.title: Positioning road-level flood sensing for disruption assessment under uncertainties using Bayesian networks
10.1016/j.ress.2026.113592.abstract: Urban flooding severely disrupts road traffic, and assessing these disruptions in a near real-time manner depends on road-level flood sensing that is usually constrained by limited financial and manpower resources. Therefore, positioning a limited number of sensing nodes requires valuing candidate locations. Yet existing strategies value locations mainly by traffic volume or local flood severity rather than disruption, and consider roads in isolation, overlooking how disruption propagates between connected roads. This study builds a double-layered Bayesian network that couples roads through their flood and traffic dependencies. A flood observed at one road then propagates to the inferred traffic disruptions across the connected network. Each candidate location is scored by the Value of Information (VoI) it contributes, combining the magnitude of the revealed traffic disruptions with how far they depart from historical expectation. A greedy algorithm then places sensing nodes where this network-wide value is the greatest. In a New York City expressway case study, the network estimates traffic speeds and the relative levels of disruption, and a few well-placed sensing nodes capture most of the attainable value. The VoI-based positioning achieves higher accumulated value than heuristics based on flood probability, traffic volume, or disruption alone. The framework is expected to help transportation and emergency agencies deploy limited flood-sensing resources where they most improve real-time traffic disruption assessment during urban floods.

10.1016/j.trac.2026.119197.title: Advances in high-specificity technology for analytical detection and diagnosis: Principles, applications and challenges
10.1016/j.trac.2026.119197.abstract: Specificity is a critical metric for evaluating pharmaceutical analysis methods. With technological advancements, highly specific analysis methods such as immunoassays, nanoenzymatic detection, aptamer recognition, molecular imprinting, and metal-organic frameworks have emerged successively. These techniques rely on biological recognition elements like antigen-antibody, enzyme-substrate, and aptamer-target interactions, enabling ultra-selective recognition and quantification of targets ranging from biomacromolecules and pathogens to heavy metal ions. Currently, these technologies are widely applied in fields such as food safety, environmental monitoring, and disease diagnosis, such as detecting pesticide residues in food, heavy metal ions in water samples, and biomarkers in blood. However, challenges remain in real-sample testing, including interference from complex matrices and the lack of unified specificity evaluation criteria, etc. This review summarizes the application of five highly specific technologies in analytical detection and diagnosis, including immunoassay, and the analytical technologies based on nanoenzyme, aptamer, MIP and MOF. Besides, we discusses the specific recognition principles, challenges and strategies, in order to provide reference for the innovation and development of methods in the field of specificity analysis.

10.1016/j.ress.2026.113709.title: A novel data-model dual-driven implicit remaining useful life prediction method for reusable thin-walled structures
10.1016/j.ress.2026.113709.abstract: Accurate remaining useful life prediction for reusable thin-walled structures is challenging because of implicit health indicators and insufficient monitoring data. To address this issue, this study proposes a data-model dual-driven implicit RUL prediction method. First, a distance correlation-based feature mapping method is developed to transform high-dimensional monitoring responses into low-dimensional features that are strongly correlated with implicit load-carrying capacity degradation. Second, a triple-uncertainty adaptive Wiener process is introduced to identify nonlinear degradation trajectories without prespecifying their functional forms, while quantifying random effects, temporal uncertainty, and measurement uncertainty. Subsequently, degradation function-constrained calibration of intrinsic structural parameters is performed, enabling indirect monitoring data to inversely update the high-fidelity structural model. Furthermore, a multi-fidelity Gaussian process model and a discrepancy correction model are employed to predict future structural performance and quantify RUL uncertainty. The results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively captures nonlinear implicit degradation, improves long-term prediction accuracy under limited monitoring data, and provides uncertainty-aware RUL estimates. This method provides an interpretable and physically constrained approach for life prediction and maintenance decision-making of reusable thin-walled structures.

10.1016/j.biotechadv.2026.109081.title: Decoding the landscape in biomanufacturing of xylose: metabolic bottlenecks and computation-assisted strategies
10.1016/j.biotechadv.2026.109081.abstract: As the second most abundant sugar in lignocellulose, xylose suffers from low utilization efficiency due to carbon catabolite repression and the scarcity of natural metabolic pathways. This bottleneck leads to the wastage of nearly 40% of available carbohydrate sources, undermining the economic competitiveness of biorefineries. Overcoming these metabolic barriers is essential for the transition toward large-scale, sustainable biomanufacturing. This review comprehensively summarizes the main pathways of xylose metabolism, with a particular focus on its major metabolic products, rate-limiting enzymes, cofactor preferences, feedback regulation, and compartmentalization. Special attention is given to the significance of modifying rate-limiting enzymes for enhancing carbon flux in the xylose metabolic pathway. The study aims to integrate current knowledge, and to provide support for further research. While enzyme limitations and redox imbalances persist, this review highlights how integrating AI-driven protein engineering with genome-scale metabolic models offers precise solutions. By optimizing key enzymes and correcting cofactor dependencies, these computational strategies provide a robust framework for overcoming metabolic bottlenecks. Ultimately, synergistic AI-metabolic modeling accelerates the efficient conversion of xylose, unlocking its transformative potential for the green bioeconomy.

10.1016/j.compositesb.2026.114366.title: Blast responses of TPU-filled hybrid sandwich panels: Experimental and numerical investigations
10.1016/j.compositesb.2026.114366.abstract: This paper investigates the blast responses and energy absorption mechanisms of hybrid sandwich panels and their constituent monolithic structures by experimental and numerical methods. Air blast tests are performed on three structural configurations, including thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) panels, metallic corrugated sandwich panels and TPU-filled hybrid sandwich panels. Numerical simulations are then carried out, with detailed constitutive models and fracture models for the different material components. A comparison is performed regarding the blast loading, damage modes and out-of-plane deformation profiles, and the discussion is conducted regarding energy absorption characteristics under different blast scenarios. Experimental and numerical results indicate that TPU filling helps suppress structural failure and preserve the overall integrity of the hybrid sandwich panel even when extensive deformation occurs. A mass-adjusted energy absorption analysis reveals the potential of the hybrid sandwich panel for enhanced energy absorption through beneficial interactions between the metallic components and TPU filler. Furthermore, parametric analyses over a stand-off distance range of 0.06-0.20 m indicate that the interaction between the metallic corrugated core and TPU filler redistributes energy absorption among the structural components, with the corrugated core and TPU filler accounting for increasingly important contributions as the blast intensity increases.

10.1016/j.ress.2026.113703.title: Resilience-constrained power system capacity expansion planning considering cascading failures
10.1016/j.ress.2026.113703.abstract: Extreme weather events can trigger cascading failures and prolonged blackouts, threatening power system resilience. Resilience-oriented capacity expansion planning is complicated by the coupling among investment decisions, cascading failure evolution, and post-event restoration, as planning decisions reshape the pre-event dispatch and power flows, thereby affecting cascading trajectories and the initial blackout states for post-event restoration. To address this challenge, this study develops a resilience-constrained capacity expansion planning framework for generation and energy storage systems (ESSs) that jointly optimizes regional capacities and bus-level resource type, location, and quantity, while accounting for disaster-induced cascading failures and system restoration. A sequential AC power flow-based simulation model is employed to capture the dynamic evolution of system outages under severe disturbances. The framework incorporates black-start and load restoration constraints and considers coordinated operation of grid-forming and grid-following ESSs. Value-at-Risk (VaR) and Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) metrics are further introduced to control the tail risk of load shedding. An iterative optimization-simulation strategy is proposed to address the endogenous dependence between planning decisions and cascading failure evolution under extreme event uncertainty, followed by a verification stage to ensure risk constraints are satisfied under the scenarios induced by the planning scheme itself. Results on the modified IEEE 39-bus system show that the proposed plan reduces the total cost by 10.76% relative to the benchmark without planning-dependent cascading-failure updates, while maintaining surviving generation output above 80% across all 20 disaster scenarios. On the IEEE 118-bus system, the number of near-total blackout scenarios is reduced from six to two across the 20 scenarios.

10.1016/j.trac.2026.119240.title: The impact of micro- and nanoplastic exposure on pregnancy and fetal health: a review of analytical and biological studies
10.1016/j.trac.2026.119240.abstract: Micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) are now widely detected across environmental and biological systems, yet their implications for human health remain poorly understood. Pregnancy represents a particularly sensitive window of exposure, during which environmental contaminants may affect maternal physiology, placental function and fetal development. This review aims to critically examine the current evidence on MNP exposure in pregnancy, with a focus on their detection in pregnancy-related tissues and fluids, their potential effects on placental biology, as well as their implications for fetal development and the maternal-exposure paradigm. We first summarise recent studies that have detected and characterised MNPs in the placenta, uterus, amniotic fluid and related biological matrices, with particular attention to vibrational spectroscopy-based approaches. We then evaluate experimental evidence showing that MNP exposure may affect placental cell viability and barrier function by inducing inflammation and oxidative stress, potentially contributing to poor fetal development with implications for intergenerational toxicity via the transmission of adverse health effects from directly exposed parents (F0) to their immediate offspring (F1). In this integrative narrative review, we highlight a field that is rapidly expanding and critically relevant, yet remains highly fragmented, methodologically inconsistent and biologically underexplored. This review aims to consolidate the current state of knowledge, identify key limitations in existing evidence, and define future research priorities for understanding the impact of MNP exposure on placental health, fetal development and pregnancy outcomes.

10.1016/j.ress.2026.113742.title: A vessel trajectory abnormal behavior classification method for cross-domain generalization and local motion pattern similarity mitigation
10.1016/j.ress.2026.113742.abstract: This paper investigates the classification of three typical anomalous maneuvering behaviors from AIS trajectories, namely looping, double U-turn, and low-speed dwelling. Such behaviors are closely associated with potential navigational risks and illicit maritime activities, and their accurate identification is essential for maritime surveillance. However, anomalous maneuvering behaviors often share similar local motion patterns while differing in global structure, leading to confusion among behavioral categories. Moreover, existing deep learning methods rely heavily on domain-specific data distributions, limiting reliability across heterogeneous maritime environments. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a vessel trajectory classification framework that improves cross-domain generalization and reduces behavioral ambiguity. The model adopts a dual-branch architecture to jointly capture local temporal dynamics and global geometric structure. A branch-level attention mechanism is further introduced to adaptively fuse the two branches, thereby alleviating the behavioral confusion caused by similar local motion patterns. To address cross-domain distribution shifts, a meta-learning training paradigm and an adaptation strategy optimized for few-shot multi-step updating are introduced, improving cross-domain adaptation in a closed-set setting where the source and target domains share a common class label space. Experiments are conducted on three cross-domain transfer scenarios. The results show that, under strong domain shift, the proposed method achieves the best performance among the compared methods while using only a few labels per class. Compared with domain adaptation and domain generalization methods that do not use target-domain labels, the proposed method attains comparable accuracy under weak shift, whereas under strong shift it achieves superior results with only a few labels.

10.1016/j.media.2026.104377.title: Depth-compensated regularization for volumetric inverse electrocardiography
10.1016/j.media.2026.104377.abstract: Objective: Accurate non-invasive localization of Premature Ventricular Contractions (PVCs) is critical for guiding catheter ablation, yet the standard inverse Electrocardiographic Imaging (ECGI) problem suffers from an inherent depth-bias that misprojects deep intramural sources onto the epicardial surface. Methods: We propose a volumetric estimation of transmembrane potentials by means of a convex optimization functional that integrates depth-compensating weights, derived from the resolution matrix of the forward operator, into both a weighted Lasso (ℓ1) penalty and a weighted Anisotropic Total Variation regularizer, with truncation stabilized by Generalized Cross-Validation. The framework is validated on 625 PVC simulations uniformly distributed throughout a biventricular myocardium, and its applicability is demonstrated on a clinical recording from a public repository comprising 21 catheter-referenced pacing sites. Results: The Weighted Lasso+Weighted TV formulation achieved a median Correlation Coefficient of 0.79 and a median Geodesic Localization Error of 6.98 mm, compared to 0.22 and 35.29 mm, respectively, for the unweighted Lasso baseline. Compared to the unweighted Lasso+TV, the inclusion of depth-compensating weights maintained comparable performance on epicardial sources while reducing the standard deviation of the Geodesic Localization Error from 28.73 mm to 4.92 mm and from 27.48 mm to 4.36 mm for myocardial and endocardial origins, respectively. On the clinical recording, the median Geodesic Localization Error of the unweighted formulation increased from 27.6 mm at non-septal pacing sites to 65.6 mm at septal ones, whereas the depth-compensated formulation remained comparable across both groups, 22.8 and 25.8 mm. Conclusion: Depth-compensated weighted regularization effectively mitigates epicardial bias in volumetric ECGI, providing a robust framework for non-invasive PVC localization without degrading superficial accuracy. Its applicability is demonstrated on a clinical recording, where the same attenuation of the depth-related bias is observed.

10.1016/j.foodhyd.2026.113569.title: Octenyl succinylation-assisted covalent polyphenol conjugation modulates the self-assembly, thermal stability, and digestibility of PSE pork myofibrillar protein
10.1016/j.foodhyd.2026.113569.abstract: Pale, soft, and exudative (PSE) pork remains a valuable protein source, however, its myofibrillar proteins (MPs) self-assemble at low ionic strength and aggregate during heating, limiting their use as functional protein ingredients, particularly in liquid foods. In this study, we combined alkaline octenyl succinic anhydride (OSA) modification of MPs with subsequent alkali-induced covalent grafting of (−)-epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG). The results showed that 8% OSA likely disrupted ordered intermolecular electrostatic associations, suppressing MP self-assembly and increasing solubility from 2.53% to 90.13% (P < 0.05). OSA pretreatment also increased EGCG binding at every concentration tested (P < 0.05), reaching 8.22 mg/g at 0.3 mM EGCG. The resulting conjugates remained highly soluble (up to 94.26%), remained well dispersed after heating at 70 °C for 30 min, and showed no visible phase separation after 7 days at higher EGCG levels (0.3 mM). The conjugates also showed stronger antioxidant activity than their non-OSA counterparts, retained high in vitro protein digestibility, and significantly increased EGCG bioaccessibility (P < 0.05). Sequential OSA modification and EGCG grafting improved MP dispersion stability during storage and resistance to heat-induced aggregation, supporting the potential use of PSE pork MPs as functional protein ingredients in low-salt formulations.

10.1016/j.compositesb.2026.114368.title: Self-damage behavior of low-textured pyrocarbon interphases boosting tensile properties of carbon/carbon composites
10.1016/j.compositesb.2026.114368.abstract: Limited utilization of intrinsic carbon-fiber strength restricts the load-bearing performance of carbon/carbon composites. Interphase controls load transfer and energy-dissipating damage, thus determining fiber-strength utilization. Here, mini-C/C composites with a control (no pre-deposited interphase) and low-textured pyrocarbon (LT-PyC) interphases of ∼100–1100 nm were studied by position-resolved electron microscopy, fiber push-in micromechanics, FIB-TEM, and tensile testing, thereby systematically elucidating the thickness-structure-performance evolution of tailored interphases. With increasing interphase thickness, a low-to-medium texture transition emerged near 900 nm, while interfacial shear strength decreased from 13.5 ± 0.6 to 6.2 ± 0.2 MPa. The failure mode transitioned from boundary-dominated debonding in the control to distributed self-damage within LT-PyC, characterized by crack deflection, branching, and diffuse microcracking in the interphase, together with step-like LT-PyC remnants and prolonged fiber pullout on fracture surfaces; the remaining LT-PyC in low-to-medium texture transition was associated with crack convergence. The approximately 500 nm interphase produced the best tensile response: strength, strain, and pre-peak strain-energy density were 2.19, 3.00, and 6.87 times the corresponding control values, respectively, while the apparent fiber-strength utilization index increased from 39 ± 3% to 84 ± 2%. These results suggest that the LT-PyC region capable of sustaining distributed intra-interphase cracking—termed here the effective self-damage volume—contributes to tensile improvement beyond the effect of local debonding strength alone. Further thickening provided diminishing damage-dissipation gains while reducing load-transfer capacity and promoting crack coalescence. Optimal performance therefore arose from balancing the effective self-damage volume of LT-PyC against retained interfacial load transfer, establishing a thickness-design principle for self-damaging interphases in load-bearing carbon/carbon components.

10.1016/j.ress.2026.113744.title: A two-stage Bayesian framework for multi-fidelity sequential updating of spatial fragility fields
10.1016/j.ress.2026.113744.abstract: This paper develops a Bayesian framework for updating event-conditioned spatial fragility fields by combining physics-informed priors with incrementally available post-disaster observations. The framework supports sequential refinement of regional vulnerability estimates as additional post-disaster evidence becomes available. The framework reformulates physics-informed fragility estimates into a Probit–Normal (PN) representation that captures aleatory variability and epistemic uncertainty in an analytically tractable form. Stage 1 performs local Bayesian updating by moment-matching PN marginals to Beta surrogates that preserve their probability shapes, enabling conjugate Beta–Bernoulli updates with soft, multi-fidelity observations. Fidelity weights encode source reliability, and the resulting Beta posteriors are re-projected into PN form, producing heteroscedastic fragility estimates whose variances reflect data quality and coverage. Stage 2 assimilates the heteroscedastic pseudo-observations through an ordered probit-warped Gaussian Process (GP) that propagates information across space and structural archetypes. A shared latent spatial severity field and strictly positive threshold-gap functions enforce pathwise ordering of exceedance probabilities and yield nonnegative exact damage-state probabilities. The framework is applied to the 2011 Joplin tornado, where wind-field priors and computer-vision damage assessments are fused under varying assumptions about tornado width, sampling strategy, and observation completeness. Controlled synthetic experiments and the Joplin application show that the framework can reduce the influence of biased priors as evidence accumulates, propagate locally updated information into unobserved regions, and produce uncertainty-aware, ordinally valid exceedance and exact damage-state probability fields.

10.1016/j.ress.2026.113620.title: An open-source toolbox for critical infrastructure generation and resilience analysis with decision-relevant applications
10.1016/j.ress.2026.113620.abstract: Critical infrastructure resilience is central to modern society, and open-source resilience toolboxes are increasingly important as domain-specific simulation engines for automated and agent-assisted scientific analysis in the AI era. Existing toolboxes have enabled diverse single- and interdependent-system studies, but many rely on detailed infrastructure data, face calibration and validation challenges under sparse observations, or separate key decision factors across fragmented workflows. We develop an open-source MATLAB toolbox for Critical Infrastructure Generation and Resilience Analysis (CIGRA) that can synthesize or augment electric power, water, gas, and road networks from population maps and optional road data, and infer missing component-specific demand and flow attributes. CIGRA further enables the identification of worst-case localized and non-localized disruption scenarios, providing a stress-testing pathway when observations are insufficient for comprehensive calibration and validation and supporting worst-case-oriented resilience planning. These capabilities are integrated with hazard cascade and component-damage scenario generation, functionality-loss calculation, restoration simulation, multiscale resilience evaluation, resilience enhancement exploration, and visualization modules to support systematic “what-if” comparisons across hazard, operating, restoration, and intervention assumptions, together with optimization-based planning. Applications of the CIGRA demonstrate an end-to-end seismic resilience analysis, how resilience measures influence resilience rankings and retrofit priorities, and how system evolution can alter system-level resilience and influence the effectiveness of retrofit strategies. CIGRA is calibration-ready and openly available at https://github.com/CICR-Lab/CIGRA.

10.1016/j.cemconcomp.2026.106890.title: Silica impregnation strategy for enhanced interfacial bonding in textile-reinforced concrete
10.1016/j.cemconcomp.2026.106890.abstract: This study investigates a silica-based textile impregnation strategy for enhancing interfacial bonding in textile-reinforced concrete (TRC). A sol-gel-derived silica precursor (SG) was compared with two conventional colloidal silica dispersions to examine how synthesis route and physicochemical properties, including particle characteristics, surface charge, solids content, rheological behavior, and surface tension, relate to bundle impregnation and bond performance of hydrophilic glass fibers and hydrophobic aramid fibers. Aramid fibers were pretreated with cationic or anionic surfactants to improve wettability and charge compatibility. Single-fiber coating and bundle penetration were examined microscopically, while bond performance was evaluated using single-bundle pull-out tests. SG and LUDOX® CL-X produced the greatest bond improvements for both fiber types and achieved comparable performance, despite the initial silica concentration of SG being approximately one-seventh that of LUDOX® CL-X. Surfactant pretreatment produced a more uniform coating on aramid fibers and improved pull-out performance. The findings link bond performance to the combined effects of fiber-silica compatibility, silica system rheology and surface tension, and coating morphology (continuous-appearing vs. particulate). Overall, SG offers an effective low-silica-content strategy for enhancing fiber-bundle bond in cementitious matrices.

10.1016/j.ress.2026.113582.title: Gas leak source localization in complex environments using a multilevel simulated annealing Bayesian–MCMC framework
10.1016/j.ress.2026.113582.abstract: Accurate gas leak source localization is essential for industrial safety monitoring and emergency response under uncertain dispersion conditions. This study develops a Bayesian inversion framework that combines Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling with multilevel simulated annealing (MLSA) initialization. Evaluation was conducted entirely using simulated data, including idealized scenarios and FLACS generated industrial concentration fields. Across 50 independent executions of the principal idealized scenario, MLSA-BMCMC achieved lower mean localization and release rate errors than B-MCMC and SA-BMCMC. Repeated noise experiments indicated adequate credible interval calibration at noise levels of 10%-30%. The FLACS cases further characterized the influence of geometric complexity on localization performance. Overall, the proposed framework provides a structured refinement of Bayesian gas leak source inversion by combining coarse to fine initialization with posterior uncertainty quantification under the tested dispersion conditions.

10.1016/j.biomaterials.2026.124736.title: Use of a c-Met-targeting aptamer-drug conjugate for efficient therapy in both primary and metastatic uveal melanoma
10.1016/j.biomaterials.2026.124736.abstract: Uveal melanoma (UM), the most common primary intraocular malignancy in adults, is associated with a high risk of metastasis, recurrence, and irreversible vision loss. However, current therapeutic options remain limited by insufficient efficacy and poor vision preservation. Building upon the molecular design of SL1-MMAE, a c-Met-targeting aptamer-drug conjugate (ApDC), here we investigate its potential translational application as a targeted therapeutic strategy for both primary and metastatic UM. SL1-MMAE exhibits high binding specificity, rapid cellular internalization, and potent cytotoxicity toward UM cells in vitro. In vivo, SL1-MMAE effectively suppresses tumor growth in both subcutaneous xenograft and liver metastasis models, significantly prolonging survival. Notably, in an orthotopic intraocular UM model, a single intravitreal injection of SL1-MMAE induces robust tumor regression without detectable ocular toxicity at the therapeutic dose. The small molecular size of the ApDC enables superior tumor penetration and reduced retention from non-target ocular tissues. These features are particularly advantageous within the confined intraocular environment, leading to enhanced therapeutic efficacy with improved safety. Compared with the clinically advanced c-Met antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) ABBV-399, the ApDC demonstrates superior antitumor activity and ocular biocompatibility for intraocular UM therapy. Nevertheless, as a preclinical study, further safety, pharmacokinetic and translational studies are warranted to better define the clinical potential of SL1-MMAE. Collectively, these findings establish c-Met-targeting ApDCs as a promising platform for the treatment of both primary and metastatic UM, offering a vision-preserving therapeutic strategy with potent antitumor efficacy and favorable safety profiles.

10.1016/j.biomaterials.2026.124739.title: Nose-to-brain delivery of multimodal nanoregulator restores metal-redox homeostasis and protects mitochondrial integrity for triple inhibitions of neuronal death in radiation-induced brain injury
10.1016/j.biomaterials.2026.124739.abstract: Radiation-induced brain injury (RIBI) has emerged as a severe complication of cranial radiotherapy, substantially impairing patients’ quality of life. Current therapies mainly rely on anti-apoptotic drugs with limited efficacy. Despite advances in understanding neuronal death in RIBI, efficient neuroprotective strategies are still lacking. Herein, we identify that beyond apoptosis, neuronal ferroptosis and cuproptosis are key drivers of RIBI. To simultaneously inhibit all three death pathways, unlike traditional approach based on small-molecular inhibitors and their combinations, we propose an innovative strategy to disrupt the vicious cycle of ROS/Fe3+/Cu2+ overload and mitochondrial dysfunction that co-drive the three cell death modalities. And a therapeutic nanodot (SPDA-SeMet) is facilely engineered by conjugating natural selenomethionine onto small-sized polydopamine nanoparticles. In RIBI mice, therapeutic outcome of SPDA-SeMet significantly outperforms neuroprotective comparator Edaravone/Dexborneol. Mechanistically, negatively-charged surface and ultrasmall size enable rapid mucus penetration and enhanced nose-to-brain delivery, and then SPDA and SeMet modules work together to restore ROS/Fe3+/Cu2+ homeostasis and preserve mitochondrial integrity in neurons via enhanced capacity in Fe3+/Cu2+ chelation, ROS scavenging, mitochondrial colocalization, thereby efficiently inhibiting neuronal apoptosis/ferroptosis/cuproptosis and inflammation. Our findings establish an essential role of neuronal ferroptosis/cuproptosis/apoptosis in RIBI pathogenesis, and provides a therapeutic nanoplatform regulating complex pathological processes for targeted therapy.

10.1016/j.cemconcomp.2026.106895.title: Scalable deposition of reactive nanoparticles for interfacial bonding of carbon textiles in cement composites
10.1016/j.cemconcomp.2026.106895.abstract: Carbon textile-reinforced concrete suffers from weak bonding at the textile/matrix interface. Concurrent synthesis–deposition of reactive nanoparticles such as nano-silica (NS), though hitherto proved useful, faces challenges with respect to scalability. To tackle this issue, we leveraged a sequential synthesis-then-deposition route built on a well-controlled sol–gel process. Microstructural analyses indicate that the two routes achieved NS deposition via distinct mechanisms: surface-assisted heterogeneous nucleation versus passive post-synthesis adsorption. The results suggest that the latter offered fewer anchoring sites and exhibited a greater tendency for particle desorption than the former. However, finer, well-defined NS particles restored a favorable adsorption–desorption balance, allowing the refined sequential route to reach near-monolayer coverage and perform on par with the benchmark. Single-roving pullout tests and interface characterization consistently trace the enhanced interfacial bonding to extended calcium silicate hydrate precipitation and interfacial transition zone densification driven by the NS-induced pozzolanic reaction. Results from uniaxial tensile tests on composite ties are also reported herein, successfully demonstrating process scalability.

10.1016/j.cemconcomp.2026.106893.title: Taguchi optimized metakaolin-based geopolymers with ionic thermoelectricity: pore structure and ion concentration coupling
10.1016/j.cemconcomp.2026.106893.abstract: This study investigated the ionic thermoelectric performance of metakaolin-based geopolymers (MK-GPs) using a Taguchi L9 orthogonal array design, in which Si/Al, Na/Al, and H2O/Na2O ratios were systematically varied to optimize multifunctional properties and develop a mechanistic understanding of thermopower generation. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) showed that the Seebeck coefficient was most strongly influenced by the Na/Al ratio, whereas long-term compressive strength was primarily determined by the Si/Al ratio. An optimal Na/Al range of 0.92-1.12 promoted stable geopolymerization, while an excessive Na/Al ratio of 1.32 reduced mechanical strength. Beyond mixture optimization, this study demonstrates that ionic thermopower in MK-GPs is driven by the synergistic coupling between ion concentration and pore network characteristics. Mixtures containing abundant mobile cations and a dense network of small capillary pores exhibited the highest Seebeck coefficient of approximately 1960 μV/°C. A regression model incorporating ion concentration in pore solution and a small capillary pore fraction captured this coupled effect, with an R2 of 0.89, indicating good agreement with the experimental data. FTIR and NMR analyses confirmed the formation of geopolymer networks, while band gap analysis indicated insulating behavior, supporting ionic transport as the dominant thermoelectric mechanism. A trade-off was observed between thermoelectric efficiency and mechanical strength, with the highest ZT achieved in specimens with lower compressive strength, whereas mechanically stronger specimens exhibited reduced thermoelectric performance. These findings establish a structure-chemistry-property relationship for ionic thermoelectricity in MK-GPs and provide a scientific basis for designing sustainable multifunctional cementitious materials for energy-harvesting applications.

10.1016/j.foodhyd.2026.113533.title: High-moisture extrusion of Alaska pollock surimi-based meat analogues: The effect of starch with different amylose and amylopectin contents on fibrous structure formation
10.1016/j.foodhyd.2026.113533.abstract: This study examined the effects of adding 4% starches with varying amylose and amylopectin contents, including high-amylose maize starch (HMS), waxy maize starch (WMS), potato starch (PS), cassava starch (CS), and mung bean starch (MS), on the fibrous structure formation in surimi-based meat analogues produced by high-moisture extrusion. Starch addition enhanced the structure and texture of the extrudates, although the degree of improvement depended strongly on the amylose and amylopectin contents. Extrudate-containing WMS exhibited the highest degree of fibrousness. Microstructural analysis revealed that WMS, PS, and CS promoted the development of continuous, compact fibrous structures, whereas HMS and MS led to the formation of loose, porous fibrous networks. Protein conformation and intermolecular interaction analyses further demonstrated that starches rich in amylopectin were more effective at promoting the transition from disordered conformations to β-sheet structures in extrudates. Additionally, these starches reduced surface hydrophobicity and enhanced disulfide and hydrogen bonding. These modifications facilitated protein aggregation and cross-linking, thereby promoting the formation of ordered fibrous structures. This study demonstrates the potential of WMS in improving fibrous anisotropy, providing a theoretical basis for the structural optimization and quality enhancement of surimi-based meat analogues.

10.1016/j.ress.2026.113756.title: A two-stage deep causal inference method with association prior for urban rail transit risk impact deduction and proactive intervention
10.1016/j.ress.2026.113756.abstract: To enhance the in-time safety management capability of urban rail transit, this paper proposes a two-stage deep causal inference framework with association prior for causal discovery and interpretable intervention in risk impact deduction. Firstly, the association rules obtained by the improved W-apriori algorithm are transformed into prior matrix, allowing causal weight to be estimated in the feasible risk evolution space and bridging the gap between statistical mining and causal inference. Next, a five-layer causal topology is reconstructed using AP-DAG-GNN, with high-weight causal relationship extracted by Pareto optimization. Then, Causal-DEMATEL and DWBC are designed to analyze node-level topological features and path-level causal cascades. Moreover, event-specific causal attribution is developed for interpretable analysis of individual high-risk emergency, identifying key causal evolution pathways and intervention nodes. To demonstrate the proposed framework, six event types are simulated using real operational data from Beijing Metro combined with baseline comparison, ablation experiment and structural stability analysis, which indicates that high-weight causal topology selected by Pareto is sensitive to random optimization and finite sample perturbations, while some key causal relationships exhibit relatively high recurrence and node importance ranking exhibits a certain degree of event dependency. These findings can not only support the effectively identification of stable risk propagation pathways and candidate intervention priorities, but also sensitively capture causal center shifts caused by specific conditions, thereby providing a foundation for early intervention, warning release, and implementation of proactive risk prevention and control strategies.

10.1016/j.pharmthera.2026.109136.title: Pharmacological targeting of ANO1/TMEM16A in cancer: from channel inhibition to protein downregulation
10.1016/j.pharmthera.2026.109136.abstract: Anoctamin 1 (ANO1/TMEM16A) is a calcium-activated chloride channel increasingly recognized as a compelling pharmacological target in oncology. Beyond its role in chloride flux, ANO1 has also been proposed to exert signaling-associated or scaffold-like functions in selected malignancies, including head and neck, breast, and lung cancers. Although pharmacological studies have progressed from broad inhibitors to selective probes and natural products, a critical need has emerged for a rigorous standard to evaluate these agents. A central challenge is distinguishing acute conductance blockade from protein-level downregulation, as these mechanisms may produce distinct biological outcomes. Channel inhibition suppresses ion flux while potentially leaving ANO1-associated protein complexes intact, whereas protein reduction may affect both conductance-dependent and signaling-associated functions; however, the extent to which these functions are mechanistically independent remains incompletely established. Consequently, regulation of ANO1 stability is emerging as a promising therapeutic strategy in tumors with high ANO1 expression and epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) activation. However, in clinically relevant EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer models, the role of ANO1 should be interpreted cautiously. Current evidence supports ANO1 as a context-dependent preclinical vulnerability rather than an established mechanism for overcoming osimertinib resistance. To address methodological inconsistencies in the field, this review summarizes ANO1 cancer pharmacology and proposes a conservative operational evidence framework. By establishing strict validation criteria, we classify ANO1 modulators into functional inhibitors, dual modulators, protein-level downregulators, and protein-stability modulators while defining evidence requirements for bona fide targeted degrader designation.

10.1016/j.ress.2026.113733.title: Design of robust multiple-layer networks for unmanned aerial vehicle communication systems
10.1016/j.ress.2026.113733.abstract: A multiple-layer UAV system includes multiple types of UAVs, and different types of UAVs are at different layers. Network robustness is used to measure the connectivity of remaining network after some nodes fail. A highly robust network can ensure that UAVs can still communicate with each other even after some UAVs fail. To improve robustness of multi-layer UAVs network, we propose a method that combines positions of UAVs and network topology. The method can be divided into two sub-methods: flight strategy and network structure. In the flight strategy, an intra-layer potential field and an inter-layer potential field are used to adjust positions of UAVs under constraints, which can reduce distance between UAVs and can enable UAVs to establish more links. Although increasing links can improve the robustness of network, the dependence of network on critical nodes has greatly increased. Once these nodes fail, the robustness of network sharply decreases. In the network structure, Deep learning method is used to search for highly robust network structure. The designed deep learning method can evenly distribute links across nodes while increasing links, thereby reducing the impact of critical nodes on network. In 3D space, experimental results show that our method can meet constraints of multi-layer UAVs network, and enables networks to have high robustness in multiple failure modes.

10.1016/j.biomaterials.2026.124733.title: Charge-neutralized anti-swelling hydrogels enable mechano-curvature-coupled microphysiological system
10.1016/j.biomaterials.2026.124733.abstract: Curvature topography and mechanical stimulation are key biophysical cues in the tissue microenvironment that play critical roles in regulating cell behavior. However, the stable construction of curved structures and the application of dynamic mechanical loading in ultrasoft biomaterials remain challenging, limiting the reconstruction of microenvironments for soft tissues such as the lung. Here, we propose a charge-neutralization anti-swelling hydrogel strategy. By introducing LiCl, Li+ ions electrostatically shield and coordinate with fixed negative charges, thereby suppressing the Donnan effect to inhibit hydrogel swelling and enhance structural stability. The resulting hydrogel exhibits a tunable Young's modulus ranging from 1.12 to 339.79 kPa. Combined with three-dimensional (3D) printing, biomimetic curved structures with curvatures ranging from 10−4 to 4 × 10−2 μm−1 were stably fabricated. Integration with a stretching driver further enabled controllable cyclic stretching (0∼40%), establishing a microphysiological system that couples curvature topography with mechanical cues and recapitulates the physiological and pathological parameters of multiple tissues. Curvature topography and mechanical stimulation significantly influenced tissue phenotypes, including surfactant secretion, proliferation, and migration, as well as drug sensitivity. This work provides a general design strategy for reconstructing complex tissue microenvironments and establishes a more physiologically relevant platform for investigating tissue development, disease mechanisms, and drug responses.
