10.1016/j.foodhyd.2026.113447.title: TGase-mediated glycosylation modified fish gelatin microgel particles stabilized high internal phase pickering emulsions: Interfacial remodeling behavior, stabilization mechanism, and 3D printing application
10.1016/j.foodhyd.2026.113447.abstract: This study explored the effects of transglutaminase (TGase)-mediated glycosylation on the interfacial remodeling behavior, microstructure evolution, and rheological properties of fish gelatins (FG) microgel particles, as well as the environmental stability and 3D printability of glycosylated FG particles-stabilized high internal phase emulsions (HIPEs) were systematically investigated. The results indicated that TGase-catalyzed glycosylation effectively regulated the particle size, molecular conformation, surface hydrophobicity, interfacial wettability and antioxidant activity of FG microgels. The optimal modification condition was obtained at an FG to chitosan oligosaccharide (COS) mass ratio of 5:1 and a TGase dosage of 20 U/g. The microgel particle size decreased to 83.87 ± 4.07 nm, surface hydrophobicity enhanced to 6176.44 ± 8.20, and the DPPH radical scavenging rate reached 63.97 ± 0.34%, which significantly improved the interfacial adsorption capacity and emulsifying performance of FG microgels. Consequently, the resultant HIPEs exhibited refined droplet size, compact interfacial structure, strengthened viscoelastic network, and improved rheological properties, including higher apparent viscosity and storage modulus. Additionally, the glycosylated FG microgel-stabilized HIPEs achieved outstanding environmental stability against thermal treatment, freeze-thaw cycles, pH variations, ionic strength, and long-term storage. The optimized structural and rheological behaviors granted HIPEs favorable extrudability, shape retention, and self-supporting capacity for high-precision 3D food printing. Mechanistically, TGase-mediated glycosylation promoted the structural unfolding of FG molecules, exposure of hydrophobic regions, and formation of covalent complexes, which facilitated the formation of dense, elastic, and robust interfacial particle networks at the oil-water interface. In conclusion, TGase-mediated glycosylation serves as an effective method to functionalize FG microgels for HIPE stabilization, offering new references for constructing edible, stable, and 3D-printable emulsions for tailor-made functional food fabrication.

10.1016/j.compositesb.2026.114373.title: Non-trade-off interlaminar fracture toughness and mechanical properties of CFRPs via low-melting temperature polyamide nano-webs
10.1016/j.compositesb.2026.114373.abstract: High-performance carbon fiber-reinforced plastic (CFRP) is attracting attention in aerospace, automotive, and pressure-vessel applications owing to its superior specific strength and stiffness. However, its brittle epoxy matrix renders CFRP susceptible to interlaminar delamination, and conventional thermoplastic interleaving typically improves fracture toughness at the expense of strength. Here, we electrospun a low-melting-temperature polyamide nanofiber web (LMPA-NW; DSC melting onset of approximately 133 °C and peak of approximately 152 °C) directly onto carbon fiber fabric and compared compression molding at 120 °C and 180 °C, using temperature-matched Pristine laminates as controls. At 120 °C, LMPA-NW/CFRP20 showed the largest improvements in initiation and propagation Mode I fracture toughness (50% and 93%), whereas LMPA-NW/CFRP30 showed a significant increase in ultimate flexural strength (23%) but non-significant increases in propagation toughness (31%) and interlaminar shear strength (5%). At 180 °C, LMPA-NW/CFRP30 showed statistically significant increases in initiation toughness (152%), propagation toughness (296%), flexural strength (20%), and interlaminar shear strength (29%), demonstrating a non-trade-off improvement. FT-IR, XPS, DSC, SEM, and TGA indicate temperature-dependent changes in the LMPA–epoxy interphase and interlayer morphology: the LMPA-NW largely retains its fibrous morphology below its melting transition, whereas it loses its fibrous structure and becomes integrated into the epoxy matrix above it. These techniques do not, however, directly establish epoxy–polyamide covalent bonding or oxidative matrix degradation, which remain to be verified.

10.1016/j.biomaterials.2026.124735.title: Mitochondria-protective polysaccharide augments burn wound repair through immunometabolic reprogramming
10.1016/j.biomaterials.2026.124735.abstract: Effective wound healing requires coordinated extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition, immune regulation, and metabolic adaptation—processes governed by fibroblast mitochondria. Conventional burn therapies fail to address the mitochondrial dysfunction that impedes tissue regeneration. Here, we show that colanic acid (CA), a microbial-derived exopolysaccharide, acts as a mitochondrial-protecting biomaterial that accelerates burn repair by restoring immuno-metabolic crosstalk. In a murine deep second-degree burn model, CA enhanced wound closure 3.1-fold over controls, reduced reactive oxidative species by 54%, and increased mature collagen deposition by 193%. Mechanistically, CA undergoes intracellular internalization with the assistance of the membrane receptor TLR4 and maintains mitochondrial integrity, evidenced by restored cristae ultrastructure, a 1.4-fold increase in oxidative phosphorylation flux, and a 1.5-fold elevation in ATP production—effects abolished upon silencing the mitochondrial regulator Thap11. Bulk RNA-seq indicated that CA reshaped the wound immune landscape by driving macrophage recruitment and M2 polarization via mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming. By synchronizing mitochondrial rescue with immune-guided ECM remodeling, CA outperformed hyaluronic acid dressings in wound closure and extracellular matrix remodeling.The preliminary translational proof-of-concept of CA was confirmed in a Bama minipig model of deep second-degree burn wound, where it enhanced re-epithelialization, angiogenesis, and tissue perfusion. Together, these findings suggest that CA is a multifunctional polysaccharide with mitochondrial protective effects capable of addressing the multifaceted pathology of burn wounds across species.

10.1016/j.foodhyd.2026.113559.title: L-Lysine synergizes with carrageenan and transglutaminase to strengthen low-salt myofibrillar protein gels through charge regulation and β-sheet-rich network consolidation
10.1016/j.foodhyd.2026.113559.abstract: Low-salt meat products often suffer from weak myofibrillar protein (MP) gelation and poor water retention. This study investigated whether L-lysine (Lys) could enhance carrageenan/transglutaminase (TGase)-assisted gelation of myofibrillar protein under low-salt conditions. Myofibrillar protein gels were prepared at 0.3 M NaCl with different Lys levels in the absence or presence of ι-carrageenan (I-Car) or κ-carrageenan (K-Car), together with TGase. Gel properties, water retention, protein dispersion, conformational changes, secondary structure, Raman spectral features, and microstructure were systematically analyzed. Lys improved low-salt gelation in a concentration-dependent manner, with the effect further modulated by carrageenan type. Among all formulations, the K-Car system containing 0.3% Lys exhibited the greatest improvement, achieving the highest gel strength (168.95 g mm) and reducing cooking loss from 60.6% to 26.5%, while forming a denser, more continuous gel network. Physicochemical analyses showed that Lys promoted protein dispersion, modified surface charge, increased surface hydrophobicity, and induced conformational unfolding, thereby facilitating subsequent network formation. FTIR analysis further indicated that K-Car more effectively directed Lys-induced protein activation toward β-sheet-rich ordered aggregation (β-sheet: 41.5% → 48.9%; PAI: 1.44 → 2.17), while Raman spectroscopy revealed enhanced disulfide-related stabilization and burial of aromatic residues. Correlation analysis suggested that gel strength and water retention were closely associated with β-sheet enrichment, reduced α-helix content, increased protein aggregation index PAI, and S–S-related Raman band intensity. These results suggest an “unfold–order–lock” mechanism in which Lys first activates myofibrillar proteins, K-Car directs ordered structural consolidation, and TGase contributes to final network stabilization. This study provides a mechanistic basis for improving the texture and moisture stability of low-salt meat protein gels through coordinated charge regulation, polysaccharide templating, and enzymatic stabilization.

10.1016/j.biomaterials.2026.124757.title: Heptamethine cyanines serve as photocaged Michael electrophiles for spatiotemporal GPX4 inhibition and ferroptosis immunotherapy
10.1016/j.biomaterials.2026.124757.abstract: Inhibiting glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) to induce ferroptosis has emerged as a crucial strategy to circumvent drug resistance. However, conventional GPX4 inhibitors, typically α-chloroacetamides, show limitations in the stability and targetability required for drug development. Here we uncover that heptamethine cyanines (Cy7) function as photocaged Michael electrophiles, enabling spatiotemporal GPX4 inhibition and ferroptosis induction with submicromolar to nanomolar potencies against both parental and drug-resistant cancer cells. The strong phototoxicity originates from the optimized electrophilicity window of the photo-uncaged Michael electrophiles, which enables selective alkylation of GPX4 selenocysteine over glutathione (GSH), thereby circumventing cellular GSH detoxification. Furthermore, the structural tunability of Cy7 dyes enables on-demand fabrication of cancer cell–specific GPX4 inhibitors, as exemplified by an enzyme-activatable Cy7 prodrug that selectively killed cancer cells in primary tumors under photoirradiation while eliciting systemic antitumor immunity to suppress distant tumors. This work establishes a new paradigm for GPX4 inhibitor development and repurposes conventional Cy7 imaging scaffolds as anticancer agents.

10.1016/j.biomaterials.2026.124754.title: Polysaccharide-confined polyaniline nanocomplexes reprogram pyrimidine metabolism for synergistic photothermal tumor ablation
10.1016/j.biomaterials.2026.124754.abstract: Polyaniline (PANI) is a promising near-infrared (NIR) photothermal agent, yet its aggregation propensity and lack of intrinsic metabolic regulatory functions restrict its in vivo antitumor application. To overcome these limitations, we engineered a biocompatible curdlan/fucoidan/polyaniline (CFP) ternary inclusion complex via a nanoconfined in-situ polymerization strategy. Utilizing the hydrophobic helical cavity of curdlan as a nano-reactor effectively regulates PANI chain growth, yielding monodispersed nanorods with superior aqueous dispersion stability. Fucoidan serves a dual role as an efficient dispersant and a potent metabolic modulator implicated in pyrimidine pathway suppression. Mechanistically, CFP enters lung adenocarcinoma cells predominantly via macropinocytosis, accounting for ∼44-47% of total internalization, with clathrin- and caveolae-mediated routes contributing only marginally. Multi-omics profiling reveals that fucoidan preferentially modulates pyrimidine metabolism, with significant down-regulation of the core enzymes TK1, DTYMK, and CDA observed at both transcriptomic and protein levels. This metabolic suppression compromises DNA damage repair capacity, rendering the massive ROS accumulation and severe DNA damage induced by PANI-based photothermal therapy largely irreversible and achieving remarkable synergistic antitumor efficacy. Bioinformatic analysis further links these metabolic genes to T cell exhaustion and immune microenvironment remodeling. In vivo, the CFP + NIR regimen exhibits prominent tumor accumulation, potent growth inhibition, and prolonged survival. Crucially, comprehensive toxicological assessments in immunocompetent mice-including hematological, serum biochemical, and histological analyses-confirm the excellent systemic biosafety of CFP. This work presents a promising strategy coupling natural polysaccharide-mediated metabolic intervention with photothermal ablation for precise tumor therapy.

10.1016/j.media.2026.104353.title: ContextMRI: Enhancing compressed sensing MRI through metadata conditioning
10.1016/j.media.2026.104353.abstract: Compressed sensing MRI seeks to accelerate MRI acquisition processes by sampling fewer k-space measurements and then reconstructing the missing data algorithmically. The success of these approaches often relies on strong priors or learned statistical models. While recent diffusion model-based priors have shown great potential, previous methods typically ignore clinically available metadata (e.g. patient demographics, imaging parameters, slice-specific information). In practice, metadata contains meaningful cues about the anatomy and acquisition protocol, suggesting it could further constrain the reconstruction problem. In this work, we propose ContextMRI, a text-conditioned diffusion model for MRI that integrates granular metadata into the reconstruction process. We train a pixel-space diffusion model directly on minimally processed, complex-valued MRI images. During inference, metadata is converted into a structured text prompt and fed to the model via CLIP text embeddings. By conditioning the prior on metadata, we unlock more accurate reconstructions and show consistent gains across multiple datasets, acceleration factors, and undersampling patterns. Our experiments demonstrate that increasing the fidelity of metadata — ranging from slice location and contrast to patient age, sex, and pathology — systematically boosts reconstruction performance. This work highlights the untapped potential of leveraging clinical context for inverse problems and opens a new direction for metadata-driven MRI reconstruction. Code is available at https://github.com/DoHunLee1/ContextMRI.

10.1016/j.compositesb.2026.114357.title: Biomimetic silk fibroin aerogel fibers with boosted thermal insulation and a flame-retardant tough shell endowed with hydrophobicity
10.1016/j.compositesb.2026.114357.abstract: Personal thermal management is important for preventing body heat loss and reducing energy consumption. Silk fibroin aerogel fibers (SAFs) are promising candidates for personal thermal management textiles, yet previously reported SAFs still face challenges such as poor mechanical properties, complex fabrication processes, and limited control over pore structures and multifunctionality. Herein, we present a detachable hollow polytetrafluoroethylene fiber template strategy to fabricate SAFs with a well-defined core-shell structure. Unlike conventional approaches, this template method allows precise regulation of the internal pore architecture (laminar, turbine-blade-like, and round-hole) simply by adjusting the silk fibroin concentration, while the polytetrafluoroethylene shell simultaneously provides high strength, knittability, and multifunctionality including flame retardancy, hydrophobicity, and electrical insulation. Heat transfer simulations further reveal the relationship between pore structure and thermal insulation. The resulting textiles exhibit superior thermal insulation, flame retardancy, and electrical insulation compared to commercial textiles such as wool, cotton, and nylon. This work offers a facile and versatile template strategy for designing high-performance, multifunctional aerogel fibers, paving the way for advanced personal thermal management textiles.

10.1016/j.compositesb.2026.114356.title: High-robust, conformally printed silver circuits on composite structures via capillary-infiltration interlocking
10.1016/j.compositesb.2026.114356.abstract: Direct printing of conductive circuits on fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) composites is highly attractive for lightweight and multifunctional aircraft structures, but it suffers from ink spreading on rough textured surfaces and weak adhesion at heterogeneous metal/polymer interfaces. Herein, a coupled interfacial reinforcement (CIR) printing strategy is proposed to fabricate high-adhesion printed nanosilver circuits on composite substrates through capillary infiltration and interfacial energy matching. An epoxy reinforcement layer is introduced to smooth the texture surface of FRP substrates and provides an interfacial energy transition, and a semi-cured polyimide/epoxy (PI/EP) infiltration layer is coated on the top before circuits printing. The infiltration layer would experience solvent-softened during silver printing and subsequently infiltrates the porous Ag layer under capillary forces during thermal curing. This process forms a mechanically interlocked Ag/PI-EP interface while preserving the continuity of the Ag conductive network. Except for the enhancement of interfacial adhesion, the CIR printing strategy also improves the printing resolution and the long-term reliability of as-printed circuits while maintaining good electrical conductivity on rough composite substrates. This printing strategy achieves an average adhesion strength of 4.87 MPa, about 5.18 times that achieved by direct Ag printing on glass fiber-reinforced polymer (GFRP). It also enables the fabrication of fine and uniform conductive lines with an average line width of 13.6 μm. Printed Ag circuits exhibit excellent durability under 500 tape-peeling cycles, soldering-tip scratching up to 300 °C, and 40 days of immersion in 5 wt% NaCl solution. Furthermore, a conformally printed electrothermal de-icing system that integrated onto an aircraft-wing exhibits rapid de-icing capability, reliable anti-icing performance, and stable cyclic operation, highlighting the potential of this generalizable interfacial reinforcement strategy for reliable printed electronics on rough composite structures.

10.1016/j.biomaterials.2026.124751.title: Orchestrating adaptive homeostasis on bioprosthetic valves: a metal-polyphenol hydrogel armor for integrated immunomodulation and endothelialization
10.1016/j.biomaterials.2026.124751.abstract: With the advancement of transcatheter valve replacement technology, bioprosthetic heart valves (BHVs) are being increasingly used in the clinical treatment of valvular diseases. However, current BHVs fail to concurrently resist thrombosis, modulate the immune and redox homeostasis in response to complex host-biomaterial interactions, leading to premature degeneration and shortened lifespan. Herein, we constructed an endothelial layer-inspired armor for BHV by fusing metal-polyphenol drug network (MPN) nanoparticle with immune/redox regulation functions and vascular endothelial glycocalyx-like layer that serve as passive defense and endothelialization scaffolds. The coating established a biomimetic endothelial defense barrier that resisted the deposition of blood components on BHVs while acting as a scaffold for endothelialization. The MPN nanoparticle fabricated through the self-assembly of Epigallocatechin-3-gallate, curcumin, and Cu2+ was anchored to endow the BHV with free-radical-scavenging capability, immunomodulatory activity and endothelialization-promoting potential. The overexpressed reactive oxygen species were scavenged and the local inflammation responses were downregulated through immune and inflammatory response pathways. This not only maintained homeostasis at the BHV bio-interface but also created a pro-endothelialization microenvironment that favors the adhesion and growth of endothelial cells. Additionally, the coating catalyzed the releasing of NO to promote the endothelialization through PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway. The combined advantages of nanoparticles and glycocalyx-like hydrogel, which integrate antithrombotic, immunomodulatory, antioxidant, endothelialization-promoting, and anti-calcification effects, provided a promising strategy to address the critical challenge of BHV degeneration.

10.1016/j.trac.2026.119228.title: Structurally tunable smart nanozymes toward decentralized sepsis diagnosis
10.1016/j.trac.2026.119228.abstract: Decentralized monitoring requires analytical platforms that translate molecular recognition in complex samples into rapid, amplified, matrix-tolerant, and clinically relevant signals. Nanozymes are emerging as smart materials because their enzyme-mimicking catalytic activity enables structurally tunable catalytic signal transduction. This review establishes dimension-dependent nanozyme catalysis as an analytical design principle for sepsis-related biomarker detection, where early assessment requires multiplexed analysis of heterogeneous, low-abundance, and dynamically varying biomarkers in complex clinical matrices. We highlight how zero-, one-, two-, and three-dimensional nanozyme architectures govern catalytic activity, signal amplification, matrix compatibility, and analytical performance across optical, electrochemical, lateral-flow, paper-based, wearable, and intelligent sensing platforms. We further identify key challenges and future priorities, including diversification of catalytic signal-generation pathways, multiplexed biomarker detection, clinical validation, reproducible nanozyme fabrication, and standardized analytical evaluation. Overall, dimension-dependent structure–activity–sensing relationships provide a framework for designing portable, dual-mode, and multiplexed nanozyme platforms for sepsis biomarker detection.

10.1016/j.compositesb.2026.114354.title: All-magneto-dielectric metasurface with ultrathin and ultra-broadband electromagnetic absorption
10.1016/j.compositesb.2026.114354.abstract: Achieving ultrabroadband electromagnetic-wave (EMW) absorption with a low profile remains a major challenge for next-generation stealth and electromagnetic-compatibility applications. Here, we develop an all-magneto-dielectric metasurface (AMDM) that synergistically combines intrinsic material loss with evanescent-wave control. FeSiCr@PVB composites with tunable dielectric and magnetic properties are first optimized to balance impedance matching and attenuation capability. Subsequently, a periodic metasurface structure is introduced to further regulate wave propagation, enabling enhanced absorption through evanescent mode excitation and near-field energy localization. Genetic algorithm optimization is employed to achieve global structural optimization, resulting in a metasurface exhibiting an ultra-broadband effective bandwidth from 1 to 24 GHz with a relative bandwidth of 184%. Full-wave simulations and experiments show consistent broadband RCS reduction. This work provides a viable strategy for decoupling and independently optimizing absorption mechanisms across different frequency regimes, offering new insights into the design of ultrathin, ultra-broadband EM absorbers.

10.1016/j.biomaterials.2026.124753.title: Energy band tunable piezoelectric nanozyme heterojunction toward cancer synergistic catalytic therapy
10.1016/j.biomaterials.2026.124753.abstract: Piezoelectric catalytic therapy (PCT) based on piezoelectric semiconductors provides a new approach for cancer therapy. Various researches have explored the construction of heterojunction structures with nanozymes to strengthen PCT effect via accelerating electron transfer kinetics and synergistic nanozyme catalysis therapy (NCT). However, limited by the fixed energy band structure of nanozymes, the selectable piezoelectric semiconductors and nanozymes with matched energy levels are few. In this work, Cu2+ engineered nanozyme MIL-100 (Fe) was self-assembled on the surface of piezoelectric material BaTiO3 (BTO) to obtain BaTiO3@MIL-100 (Fe, Cu) (BTO@Fe-Cu) nanoparticles (NPs) with flexible heterojunction types, which presented synergetic NCT and PCT effect. Theoretical calculations revealed that Cu2+ introduced a new 3d orbital in the Fe-O structure, which altered the charge transfer pathways and enhanced the dual-enzyme activity of MIL-100 (Fe). Lattice distortion further modulated the valence band gap and transformed the heterostructure from type-Ⅰ to type-S for high electron-hole separation efficiency. BTO@Fe-Cu NPs fundamentally intensified the efficiency of NCT and PCT, which synergistically activated the ferroptosis/cuproptosis pathways. Moreover, scRNA-seq analysis indicated treatment-associated changes in immune-cell composition and transcriptional states. Together with the immunophenotyping results, these findings supported the potential of the piezoelectric nanozyme for the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) regulation.

10.1016/j.biomaterials.2026.124750.title: Engineering hypoactivated platelet-derived coating to decouple thrombosis for vascular regeneration
10.1016/j.biomaterials.2026.124750.abstract: The clinical performance of intravascular stents remains limited by thrombotic complications and delayed vascular healing. While cell membrane-based coatings have been explored to recapitulate native biointerfaces, achieving simultaneous hemocompatibility and pro-regenerative functionality remains challenging due to the intrinsic thrombogenicity of platelet-derived materials. Here, we propose a brand-new hypoactivated platelet-derived coating (hPLC) by sequentially assembling fibrin networks and low-activated platelets, followed by controlled lysis to remove pro-thrombotic components. This approach preserves the structural and biointerfacial features of platelet membrane while decoupling thrombogenic activity from regenerative functionality. The resulting hPLC endows materials with reduced protein adsorption, suppressed coagulation, and attenuated inflammatory responses. Transcriptomic analysis further reveals that hPLC enhances endothelial compatibility through coordinated regulation of anti-apoptotic, cytoskeletal remodeling, and angiogenic pathways. In vivo stent implantation studies demonstrate that hPLC-coated stents provide a pro-regenerative microenvironment, significantly accelerating re-endothelialization while inhibiting neointimal hyperplasia and peri-strut inflammation. These findings establish a bioinspired and clinically translatable strategy for engineering multifunctional vascular interfaces from readily available blood components, offering a versatile platform for the surface engineering of vascular devices.

10.1016/j.ress.2026.113701.title: Risk response decisions for critical infrastructures in complex interdependent scenarios: A data-intelligence-driven integrated model
10.1016/j.ress.2026.113701.abstract: Critical infrastructures (CIs) are often exposed to multiple risks whose consequences may be aggravated or mitigated by both CI interdependency and risk interdependency, making the modeling of risk response decisions (RRDs) more challenging under limited and heterogeneous information. This study aims to develop a data-intelligence-driven RRD model that links preparedness, detection/diagnosis, and treatment decisions through a shared ontology representation. First, an RRD ontology is constructed from multi-source text data and expert knowledge to organize reusable scenario, criterion, strategy, and rule knowledge. Subsequently, a dual-interdependency and criterion-adaptive mechanism is employed to quantify the realistic scenario by combining predefined information with on-site observations and interdependency-effect information, in which aggregation is configured according to the interdependency and cumulative characteristics of individual criteria. Following the scenario diagnosis, ontology-based case retrieval is conducted, and the extracted strategies enter a rule-guided post-retrieval adaptation process involving effect screening, coverage checking, and strategy coordination. Furthermore, a case study on the “7.21 Beijing Torrential Rain” is conducted. Sensitivity, ablation, and retrospective analyses examine the local stability of the decision results, the effects of interdependency modeling and rule-guided adaptation, and the correspondence between generated actions and documented historical responses. This study provides case-specific evidence for the feasibility, incremental decision value, and practical relevance of the proposed model for RRDs in complex interdependent CI scenarios.

10.1016/j.biomaterials.2026.124752.title: Bio-orthogonally functionalized biomimetic nanoreactors suppress lung cancer stem-like cells by triggering a self-amplifying endoplasmic reticulum-mitochondria stress loop
10.1016/j.biomaterials.2026.124752.abstract: The compensatory signal transmission between the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and mitochondria maintains the survival of lung cancer stem cells (LCSCs). This study designed a bio-orthogonally functionalized biomimetic nanoreactor to dissociate this protective crosstalk and induce a self-amplifying stress feedback loop. By integrating an N-cadherin-targeting aptamer with tumor membrane masking technology, this nanoreactor achieves enhanced specificity for LCSCs targeting. The nanoreactor is loaded with the photosensitizer TAPP and bortezomib (BTZ). Upon laser irradiation, TAPP generates reactive oxygen species (ROS) locally, rapidly collapsing the mitochondrial membrane potential and inducing oxidative injury. Concurrently, BTZ inhibits the proteasome, blocking the degradation of ubiquitinated proteins and triggering acute ER stress, which promotes Ca2+ release into mitochondria and further exacerbates mitochondrial damage. In turn, damaged mitochondria release mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), aggravating ER dysfunction and establishing a self-amplifying vicious cycle between the ER and mitochondria that progressively escalates cellular damage. Additionally, treatment was accompanied by reduced STAT3 phosphorylation and decreased expression of stemness-associated markers, alongside ER–mitochondrial dysfunction and enhanced cytotoxicity in stem-like cells.

10.1016/j.ress.2026.113736.title: Time-dependent reliability analysis of anchored slopes under varying seismic intensities and allowable displacement criteria
10.1016/j.ress.2026.113736.abstract: This study proposes an integrated time-variant reliability analysis framework incorporating varying seismic intensities and performance-based allowable displacement (AD) criteria. A 12-m-high anchored slope was investigated using four sets of non-stationary random ground motion samples with different Peak Ground Acceleration (PGA) levels. The systematic analysis examined the influence of seismic intensity on slope acceleration response, anchor axial force variation, and permanent displacement characteristics. The Probability Density Evolution Method (PDEM) was used to track the probability density evolution of crest permanent displacement, quantifying time-varying failure probability under various displacement thresholds. The numerical framework is validated against a large-scale shaking-table test of an anchored slope and benchmarked against Monte Carlo simulation, jointly confirming the modeling accuracy and computational efficiency of the proposed approach. Results indicate that slope dynamic responses are highly sensitive to seismic intensity and exhibit significant spatial variability. Acceleration and permanent displacement are markedly amplified at the slope crest and surface compared to the interior. Strong motions increase response uncertainty, leading to nonlinear time-dependent displacement accumulation. Anchor axial forces exhibit significant spatial heterogeneity, with toe anchors sustaining the highest loads during high-intensity earthquakes. Failure probability is governed jointly by PGA and AD thresholds, while the mainshock phase constitutes a critical window for abrupt failure probability escalation. The study offers guidance for the seismic design and reliability assessment of anchored slopes in high-intensity regions.

10.1016/j.foodhyd.2026.113561.title: Cold oxygen plasma engineering of chitosan-zein bilayer interfaces: Adhesion mechanisms and functional performance
10.1016/j.foodhyd.2026.113561.abstract: Weak interfacial adhesion limits the performance of multilayer biopolymer films assembled from chemically dissimilar components. This study investigated cold oxygen plasma as a surface-selective strategy for strengthening chitosan-zein bilayers without a chemical compatibilizer or tie layer. Preformed chitosan films were plasma-treated for 2, 4, or 8 min before zein deposition, and the resulting changes in surface chemistry, wettability, interfacial morphology, adhesion, and composite performance were evaluated. Plasma exposure progressively oxidized the chitosan surface, increasing the O/C ratio from 0.43 to 0.56 and introducing additional C–O- and O=C–O-containing environments while largely preserving the bulk polymer structure. The water contact angle decreased from 88.18° to 37.96°, whereas total surface free energy increased from 42.45 to 64.82 mN/m; this increase was driven primarily by a more than 13-fold rise in the polar component. Cross-sectional microscopy revealed a continuous interfacial gap in the untreated bilayer, while plasma-treated films exhibited compact, continuous boundaries. Correspondingly, T-peel strength increased monotonically from 0.14 to 1.39 N/25 mm, representing an almost tenfold increase after 8 min. The enhanced interface also reduced water vapor and oxygen permeability by approximately 57% and 51%, respectively, relative to the untreated bilayer and increased elongation at break, although tensile strength did not differ significantly among the bilayer groups. DSC profiles remained broadly unchanged, indicating that plasma modification was consistent with the absence of substantial changes in bulk thermal-transition behavior. The findings demonstrate that plasma-induced oxidation and improved wetting can transform a weakly laminated chitosan-zein structure into an integrated bilayer with improved adhesion and barrier performance.

10.1016/j.ress.2026.113665.title: Spatio-temporal task selection and mission abort decisions during multi-task execution under stochastic degradation
10.1016/j.ress.2026.113665.abstract: This study investigates a degrading mobile system that sequentially executes multiple spatially distributed tasks, while balancing the conflicting objectives of mission success and system survival. Mission abort policies define conditions under which a mission should be aborted to avoid severe economic losses and safety hazards caused by system failure. In many real-world missions, particularly those involving a single system performing sequential tasks, the ability to adapt both task sequences and abort timing in response to real-time system health is critical. However, relatively few studies have investigated mission abort policies in such multi-task settings. In this study, each task is represented as a position vector on a two-dimensional plane, and the mission trajectory is discretized into equal-length segments using a predefined spatial interval, thereby generating regular decision epochs along the execution path. Decision-making is based on the system state, including the degradation level, current position, and task progress. The focus of this study is on integrating intermediate mission abort decisions with dynamic task selection in a multi-task setting. This framework enables dynamic decisions between task continuation and mission abort during execution, as well as between task selection and mission abort at task completion. The resulting problem is formulated as a Markov decision process, and the value functions are explicitly derived to characterize the optimal policy. The structural properties of the optimal policy are established, including the monotonicity of the value function and the degradation-threshold structure of the mission abort decision under a safe-return assumption. Extensive sensitivity analyses further demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed policy across different parameter settings, spatial layouts, and numbers of tasks, while providing evidence of its robustness and computational scalability over the problem settings considered.

10.1016/j.ress.2026.113794.title: Incentivized coordinated resilient scheduling for multi-microgrids: an asymmetric Nash bargaining approach considering peer-to-peer trading and differentiated demand response
10.1016/j.ress.2026.113794.abstract: Extreme events may force interconnected multi-microgrid systems into islanded operation, resulting in severe power shortages and operational challenges. Under such conditions, enabling resilient and incentive-compatible cooperation among self-interested microgrids through peer-to-peer trading remains an important research issue. To this end, a coordinated resilient scheduling framework based on asymmetric Nash bargaining is proposed for interconnected multi-microgrids, incorporating differentiated demand response to exploit the heterogeneous flexibility of data center batch workloads, industrial processes, and thermostatically controlled loads. The proposed framework consists of a social welfare maximization problem and a profit allocation problem, where asymmetric bargaining factors are introduced to reflect the contributions of participating microgrids. A tailored projection function based alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) is further developed to solve the resulting mixed-integer nonlinear programming problem in a distributed manner while preserving microgrid privacy. Case studies on the IEEE 33-bus and IEEE 123-bus systems show that the proposed framework effectively reduces operating costs and load shedding, verifying its effectiveness and scalability.

10.1016/j.biomaterials.2026.124755.title: Endothelium-targeted myc silencing suppresses pathological ocular neovascularization
10.1016/j.biomaterials.2026.124755.abstract: Ocular neovascularization (NV) causes blindness, yet anti-VEGF therapy has limited efficacy. Myc controls endothelial cell (EC) proliferation and activation, however, its pathological role in ocular NV and therapeutic value remain unclear. In this study, we found that Myc was markedly upregulated in neovascular ECs (NV-ECs). Mechanistically, glycolytic reprogramming drove the hexosamine biosynthetic pathway (HBP), promoting Myc O-GlcNAcylation, which stabilized Myc protein. Endothelial-specific Myc knockout significantly suppressed EC proliferation, thereby alleviating NV progression and preserving visual function. To target Myc therapeutically, we engineered an endothelium targeted, cell membrane hybridized lipid nanoparticle encapsulating Myc siRNA (Lip@siMyc). This system achieved homotypic targeting, vitreal penetration, and sustained Myc gene silencing, and markedly inhibited ocular NV in mice. Notably, Lip@siMyc showed efficacy comparable to aflibercept, and combined treatment produced enhanced anti angiogenic effects. In summary, our findings establish the glycolysis/HBP/Myc axis as a critical regulator of EC proliferation and highlight endothelial Myc blockade as a promising therapeutic strategy for ocular NV.

10.1016/j.compositesb.2026.114376.title: Breaking through the robustness-transparency tradeoff in polymer composites by fractal interfaces
10.1016/j.compositesb.2026.114376.abstract: Transparent and robust polymer composites remain rare because the interfaces required for mechanical reinforcement also strongly scatter light. Here we show that this tradeoff can be broken through by replacing conventionally smooth filler/matrix interfaces with fractal interfaces. In poly(vinyl alcohol) composites reinforced with hyper-branched nanoparticles, this design delivers a high tensile modulus (∼3.3 GPa) with exceptional ductility (∼240% fracture strain) and a toughness of ∼188 MJ m−3, while achieving an absolute average visible transmittance of ∼86% over 400–800 nm (at 30 μm film thickness), retaining ∼95% of the average visible transmittance of pristine poly(vinyl alcohol) (∼90.5%). The deformation morphology is consistent with distributed damage, while the optical response is discussed in terms of an effective-medium interpretation of the polymer-associated hyper-branched silica nanoparticles (HBSP) framework. These findings suggest the potential of open, polymer-associated silica architectures for combining tensile reinforcement with high visible-light transmission in compatible polymer systems.

10.1016/j.ress.2026.113700.title: Simulating dynamic transport-economic interdependencies for post-earthquake regional economic recovery
10.1016/j.ress.2026.113700.abstract: Infrastructure disruptions from natural hazards can generate substantial indirect economic losses through complex, time-dependent interdependencies between physical systems and regional economies. Systematic quantification of these propagation mechanisms is essential for developing actionable mitigation and recovery strategies that maximize societal benefits. This study develops a dynamic modeling framework that explicitly links transport system disruptions, including road networks and ports, to regional economic performance through physical constraints on labor and freight mobility. The framework integrates hazard simulation, physical system damage and recovery modeling, and a refined Adaptive Regional Input–Output (R-ARIO) model to dynamically simulate sectoral economic activities as physical disruptions evolve over time. We apply the framework to evaluate the indirect economic impacts of transport system disruption in the San Francisco Bay Area under a magnitude 7.3 Hayward earthquake scenario. Besides the direct building damage of $47.9 billion, the model estimates that transport system disruption can generate an additional $3.3 billion indirect economic loss on top of the $62.3 billion indirect loss attributed to building damage. Road network and port disruptions exhibit distinct temporal effects on regional economic performance, with varying sensitivities across economic sectors. Moreover, the physics-based integration enables the identification of sector-specific bottlenecks and associated critical periods introduced by each transport system during recovery, providing actionable insights for targeted mitigation and resilience planning to reduce cascading economic impacts.

10.1016/j.foodhyd.2026.113553.title: Formulation and characterization of a xanthan–galactomannan hydrogel loaded with soy protein-stabilized oil droplets for controlled texture design
10.1016/j.foodhyd.2026.113553.abstract: Emulsion gels are promising foods for at-risk populations because they can provide essential nutrients while facilitating safe swallowing. This study examined the effects of xanthan gum (XG), locust bean gum (LBG), guar gum (GG), and calcium lactate (CL) on the physicochemical properties of soybean protein isolate (SPI)-stabilized emulsion gels. Nine XG–LBG–GG formulations and four CL concentrations were tested at a total gum concentration of 1% (w/w). Each formulation contained 1.5% (w/w) oil droplets (d4,3 = 21.45 μm) and 2.8% (w/w) SPI-derived soluble solids. Texture profile analysis, rheology, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, and syneresis analysis were performed. SPI addition decreased hardness, cohesiveness, and G′, while subsequent oil incorporation decreased adhesiveness and G′ and increased syneresis. Gum composition mainly affected hardness and storage modulus (G′), and the XG–LBG blending term showed a significant positive effect on both. In the CL experiment, hardness and cohesiveness increased at 0.15% CL, higher G′ was maintained over 25–70 °C, and syneresis decreased significantly at 0.10–0.15% CL (p <0.05). Changes in O–H/N–H absorbance were partly consistent with the physical property results but did not clearly explain composition-dependent structural changes. Oil droplet size in the representative formulation remained stable during two weeks of storage, and all emulsion gels were classified as the International Dysphagia Diet Standardization Initiative (IDDSI) level 4. These findings can provide a food-engineering basis for controlling the physical and water-holding properties of SPI-stabilized emulsion gels for future texture-modified foods for dysphagia.

10.1016/j.ress.2026.113781.title: How do hazard–exit–behavior interactions amplify risk in classroom earthquake evacuation?
10.1016/j.ress.2026.113781.abstract: Classroom earthquake evacuation is a time-critical safety problem because evolving non-structural hazards can simultaneously constrain exit functionality and alter pedestrian responses. Existing models often treat environmental hazards, exit conditions, and adaptive behavior separately, limiting their ability to explain how localized seismic disruption propagates into congestion and hazard exposure. This study develops a mechanism-oriented hazard–exit–behavior coupling framework integrating fragility-driven hazard generation, time-varying exit-capacity degradation, stress-responsive movement adjustment, utility-based exit choice, and dynamic path replanning. The framework is evaluated through empirical speed–density comparison, adaptive-speed ablation, component-level verification, and progressive coupling comparison. Results show that seismic excitation alone causes limited degradation, whereas falling hazards substantially increase evacuation delay and exposure. The 95th-percentile evacuation time rises from 15.46 s in the baseline and dynamic-hazard-only cases to 56.73 s with exit degradation and 81.70 s under full coupling. Meanwhile, 95th-percentile hazard exposure decreases from 51.14 s to 47.89 s from exit degradation to full coupling, indicating behavioral redistribution of congestion and exposure. Hazards concentrated near exits cause greater degradation than spatially dispersed hazards. These findings identify a risk-amplification pathway linking localized hazards, exit degradation, behavioral adaptation, and congestion evolution.

10.1016/j.biomaterials.2026.124713.title: Ultrasound-programmable poly(amino acid) nanocomposite enables synchronized metal ion−cisplatin release to overcome multidrug resistance
10.1016/j.biomaterials.2026.124713.abstract: Although immunotherapy has demonstrated remarkable clinical anti-cancer efficacy, chemotherapy remains the most widely used therapeutic modality. Multidrug resistance (MDR) remains a major barrier to platinum-based chemotherapy and is closely associated with insufficient intracellular drug accumulation, elevated antioxidant capacity, and impaired stress responsiveness in cancer cells. Here, an ultrasound (US)-programmable poly(amino acid) nanocomposite, EG-KFc20-KSA/CDDP, is developed to enable synchronized intracellular release of Fe(II) and cisplatin (CDDP) for coordinated chemoresistance reversal. Under US irradiation, EG-KFc20-KSA/CDDP accelerates the release of Fe(II) and CDDP in tumor microenvironments (TMEs), triggering overproduction of intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) and amplifying oxidative stress. In CDDP-resistant A549DDP lung caner cells, EG-KFc20-KSA/CDDP elevates ROS levels by 2.7-fold and reduces glutathione (GSH) levels to 31.2% of those in the Control group. Further mechanistic investigation reveals that the robust intracellular oxidative stress and associated mitochondrial damage also enhance autophagic activity, as evidenced by a marked increase in autolysosome formation. EG-KFc20-KSA/CDDP combined with US achieves an 85.3% tumor inhibition rate and prolongs the survival of A549DDP tumor-bearing mice to 61 days in vivo. This study establishes a US-programmable metal ion/chemotherapeutic co-delivery strategy that integrates oxidative stress amplification with chemotherapy and provides a mechanistically supported strategy for overcoming MDR.

10.1016/j.ress.2026.113789.title: A multi-level dependability model for structural degradation composition and resource prioritisation in cybersecurity service networks
10.1016/j.ress.2026.113789.abstract: Dependability assessment of interconnected service infrastructures requires the local degradation of individual services to be integrated with the structural dependencies through which their system-wide effects accumulate. Existing approaches typically analyse queueing performance, resilience, structural criticality, and resource allocation separately, thereby providing limited support for compositional system-level assessment. This study proposes a multi-level dependability model for an open network of cybersecurity services that combines local stochastic dynamics, routing-weighted structural degradation composition, and cost-aware resource reinforcement. Each service is represented as a hysteresis-controlled GI/M/1 node with renewal arrivals and two-rate exponential service. Local stationary degradation measures are transformed through a non-negative compositional network operator to obtain a global degradation functional and a normalised dependability indicator. A structural-functional sensitivity criterion is then derived to prioritise service reinforcement according to the predicted reduction in global degradation per unit cost. Controlled local verification using renewal inputs matched to node-level arrival summaries from CIC-IDS2017 and UNSW-NB15 yielded a Spearman correlation of 0.99983 and a mean absolute error of 0.00579 events for the time-stationary mean number in the system. Relative to a resource-equivalent fixed-rate model, median relative error decreased from 11.8% to 5.0% and from 13.9% to 5.8%. The proposed framework provides an analytically grounded basis for dependability assessment and resource prioritisation in structurally interdependent service networks.

10.1016/j.cemconcomp.2026.106892.title: Functional cement-based materials with interfacial solar evaporation capability for seawater desalination and sustainable construction water supply
10.1016/j.cemconcomp.2026.106892.abstract: Freshwater scarcity and chloride exposure constrain cement-based construction in coastal regions. Here, a directionally porous cement composite was developed for interfacial solar evaporation of seawater, and the collected condensate was evaluated as mixing and curing water for mortar. The composite was fabricated by directional freezing and freeze-drying of a cement–hydroxypropyl methylcellulose matrix, followed by application of a Ti2O3/PEDOT:PSS photothermal coating. After 28 d of curing, the composite retained vertically aligned channels, exhibited a solar-weighted absorptance of 94.1%, reached 60.7 °C under one-sun irradiation, and had dry and water-saturated thermal conductivities of 0.177 and 0.580 W m−1 K−1, respectively. Mercury intrusion porosimetry showed age-dependent evolution of mercury-accessible pores, while Raman spectroscopy and differential scanning calorimetry revealed differences in pore-water hydrogen bonding and thermal response. These observations were consistent with the reduced configuration-dependent equivalent evaporation enthalpy of the 28 d composite (581.1 J g−1). At a 5 cm exposure height, the top-area-normalized evaporation rate reached 3.458 kg m−2 h−1. Rejection exceeded 98.67% for six measured ions (Na+, Mg2+, K+, Ca2+, Cl−, and SO42−), and the condensate pH was 7.23. Condensate-water and seawater mortars showed 28 d compressive strengths of 45.5 and 43.6 MPa, respectively. After fixed-voltage accelerated exposure, steel in condensate-water mortar showed fewer visible corrosion products and a higher representative fitted charge-transfer resistance than in seawater mortar, indicating lower corrosion tendency under the test conditions. These results demonstrate the feasibility of solar-driven water production and condensate reuse in cementitious materials and provide a basis for more scalable, energy-efficient fabrication routes.

10.1016/j.ress.2026.113746.title: Optimal maintenance and abort policies for mission-critical systems with heterogeneous mission severity
10.1016/j.ress.2026.113746.abstract: Many mission-critical systems must complete an ordered sequence of missions under uncertain deterioration and mission-dependent operating severity. Before each mission, the operator may start directly, perform maintenance to restore system health, or abort the remaining sequence. For heterogeneous mission profiles, the decision is difficult because mission severity affects failure risk, the post-mission health distribution, and the value of repairing the system for later missions. Existing studies optimize mission abort or maintenance separately, with limited attention to their joint design in multi-mission sequences with varying severity. This study develops a joint maintenance and mission abort policy for a mission-critical system subject to multiple heterogeneous missions. We formulate the problem as a finite-horizon Markov decision process (MDP) and derive structural properties showing that the optimal value is monotone in system health and mission severity, the abort decision follows a threshold structure, and severity changes the relative attractiveness of maintenance and direct continuation. Based on these properties, we develop an improved backward induction algorithm that prunes unnecessary state–action evaluations. Numerical examples show that the proposed policy achieves a lower expected total cost than benchmark policies, while the improved algorithm reduces computation time across the tested problem sizes.

10.1016/j.ress.2026.113743.title: DERF: Dynamic evolution risk field-based risk assessment for pedestrian-vehicle potential collision
10.1016/j.ress.2026.113743.abstract: Accurate and timely assessment of pedestrian-vehicle collision risk is fundamental to the reliability and safety assurance of autonomous driving systems. In urban traffic, inadequate modelling of pedestrian-vehicle interactions and lagging risk perception leave pedestrians vulnerable. To address this, the paper introduces a dynamic evolving risk field (DERF) method and develops a collision volume model using bounding boxes to enable effective trajectory crossing detection. Temporal risk is quantified by fusing time difference to collision and time to last arrival, while spatial risk is modelled via cusp catastrophe theory to capture nonlinear transitions from gradual to acute states. A multilayer perceptron nonlinearly fuses these features into spatiotemporal interaction factors, combined with a direction-sensitive modulation function, enabling real-time smooth evolution of risk field intensity and distribution. Experiments on the pedestrian-vehicle interaction dataset show that our method achieves 0.92 accuracy at a 1 s prediction horizon and 38.5 FPS, outperforming state-of-the-art in accuracy, recall, and operation speed. The results confirm that our approach delivers reliable risk estimates with balanced precision and recall, supporting reliable safety assessment under dynamic and uncertain traffic conditions.

10.1016/j.trac.2026.119241.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of recent analytical methodologies applied in the determination of emerging and persistent organic contaminants in PM2.5
10.1016/j.trac.2026.119241.abstract: This review provides a critical assessment of recent analytical methodologies for determining four classes of emerging and persistent organic contaminants (EPOCs) (flame retardants, plasticizers, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances [PFAS], and polychlorinated biphenyls [PCBs]) in fine particulate matter (dp) up to 2.5 μm (PM2.5). A systematic literature search following the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) protocol retrieved 74 relevant studies published between 2019 and 2025. Sampling strategies were predominantly based on outdoor campaigns using high-volume samplers. Sample preparation and analytical workflows showed notable class-specific patterns: for instance, acidic pH and negative ionization modes (NCI/ECNI) were common in methods halogenated flame retardants and PCBs, while PFAS analysis often relied on specialized solid-phase extraction sorbents. A wide range of chromatographic systems was observed, with gas and liquid chromatography frequently coupled to tandem or high-resolution mass spectrometry. A meta-analysis of 161 data points from five studies on PFAS, using a random-effects multilevel model with restricted maximum likelihood (REML) estimation, revealed a combined average recovery rate of 98%. However, high heterogeneity was observed, strongly influenced by the analytes and the experimental conditions. Future research should focus on multicomponent approaches, automation, miniaturized extraction techniques, and environmentally sustainable workflows to improve efficiency, comparability, and analytical comprehensiveness in atmospheric studies.

10.1016/j.ress.2026.113676.title: Optimal condition-based maintenance and inspection strategy under imperfect condition monitoring: Relevance of the partially observable Markov decision process framework
10.1016/j.ress.2026.113676.abstract: Condition-based maintenance (CBM) strategies rely on the condition monitoring of a given asset to schedule maintenance interventions. In this article, we focus on a system with multiple degraded states and seek to compute the optimal CBM policy when two sources of monitoring information are available to the decision-maker. On the one hand, we consider that a continuous monitoring system is implemented, providing free but imperfect information. On the other hand, the decision-maker may decide to schedule costly but perfect inspections, revealing exactly the true degradation state of the item. We model the problem as a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP), where preventive maintenance actions should be wisely planned in order to reduce the likelihood of expensive failures and corrective maintenance interventions. We show that the POMDP framework is a convenient way when dealing with imperfect information. POMDP may be difficult to solve, but we compare two concurrent solving approaches and illustrate to what extent modern solvers have improved and enabled them to solve such problems efficiently. Finally, we propose a sensitivity analysis on the performance of the condition monitoring system and suggest that such a framework could be very helpful in estimating the value of information (VoI) that could be expected from the implementation of sensing technologies with a certain average accuracy. We further quantify the value of perfect inspections and show that monitoring and inspections act as substitutes.

10.1016/j.compositesb.2026.114370.title: Dual-channel regulation of electrospun high-entropy carbide/carbon fibrous films for high-performance electromagnetic interference shielding
10.1016/j.compositesb.2026.114370.abstract: Lightweight electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding films for thermally exposed environments require not only high shielding effectiveness, but also stable macroscopic conductive networks and sufficient internal attenuation under high-temperature air conditions. Here, electrospun high-entropy carbide/carbon fibrous films are developed to address this challenge through a dual-channel shielding strategy. Entropy-guided multicomponent compositional design in the high-entropy (TiZrHfNbTa)C/carbon framework promotes distributed carbide formation, suppresses localized particle coarsening, and preserves the carbon-derived fibrous backbone, thereby constructing an efficient conductive network across the freestanding film. On this basis, nitrogen regulation may introduce additional polarization-related attenuation through N-related defects, polar C–N/M − N bonding environments, and carbide/carbon interfacial heterogeneity. The optimized HEC@5 N fibrous film achieves an ultrahigh average EMI shielding effectiveness of 118.2 dB in X-band (8.2–12.4 GHz) at a thickness of only 0.8 mm and retains 108.6 dB during in situ high-temperature testing in air after stabilization at 600 °C. These results demonstrate the potential of dual-channel regulation in electrospun high-entropy carbide/carbon fibrous films for achieving high-efficiency EMI shielding under elevated-temperature conditions.

10.1016/j.metabol.2026.156820.title: Functional and body composition outcomes of pharmacological interventions for sarcopenia in older adults: A systematic review and pairwise meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
10.1016/j.metabol.2026.156820.abstract: Background & aims Pharmacological trials in sarcopenia have reported changes in muscle mass or selected functional measures, but the consistency and clinical importance of these effects remain uncertain. We conducted a systematic review and pairwise meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in adults aged ≥65 years. Methods The original review search used MEDLINE and Embase from inception to 9 February 2026. ClinicalTrials.gov was checked immediately after completion of the systematic review. Interventions were analyzed within four broad therapeutic Groups and complementary pharmacological Classes. Random-effects pairwise meta-analyses used mean differences (MDs) for functional outcomes and Hedges' g standardized mean differences (SMDs) for body-composition outcomes. Results Twenty-six RCTs including 3237 participants were included. At the Group level, Hormonal and anabolic therapies showed small pooled differences in grip strength (MD 1.003 kg, 95% CI 0.007 to 2.000) and 6-minute walk distance (MD 12.335 m, 95% CI 5.043 to 19.627). Myostatin inhibitors showed a gait-speed difference of 0.0300 m/s (95% CI 0.0295 to 0.0305) and a single-study estimate for appendicular lean body mass (SMD 0.573, 95% CI 0.291 to 0.855). The functional differences were below commonly cited meaningful-change benchmarks. Class-level evidence was sparse, with several Classes represented by one trial. Functional estimates for RAAS-based and Metabolic therapies were based on few trials and varied across outcomes. Conclusion Functional and body-composition estimates varied across therapeutic Groups and Classes. The observed functional differences were small relative to commonly cited benchmarks, and Class-level evidence was sparse. Future trials should prioritize durable mobility, independence, and safety outcomes.

10.1016/j.foodhyd.2026.113570.title: Iron saturation modulates interfacial rearrangement and thermal aggregation of lactoferrin–β-lactoglobulin complexes: Consequences for iron partitioning during digestion
10.1016/j.foodhyd.2026.113570.abstract: Iron saturation of lactoferrin (LF) is an intrinsic determinant of its conformation and may further regulate its interactions with other milk proteins during processing and digestion. LF and β-lactoglobulin (βlg) coexist in whey-based dairy systems and can associate through electrostatic and other non-covalent interactions. However, whether iron-induced conformational changes in LF further affect LF–βlg association, thermal aggregation, and subsequent iron partitioning during digestion remains unclear. This study examined how iron saturation affects the structure, thermal aggregation, proteolysis, and iron partitioning during digestion of LF–βlg complexes using spectroscopic and physicochemical analyses, in vitro gastrointestinal digestion, protein–protein docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Increasing iron saturation was associated with lower surface hydrophobicity and accessible free thiol content of LF–βlg complexes, together with greater resistance to heat-induced aggregation. After heating at 57.5 °C, the particle size of Apo-LF–βlg (AB) increased to 6700 nm and retained 67.30% soluble protein, whereas the particle size of Holo-LF–βlg (HB) remained at 234 nm with 88.13% soluble protein retention. Higher iron saturation also reduced proteolytic susceptibility and altered iron partitioning among soluble and <3 kDa ultrafiltrable fractions. Gastric digestion promoted iron transfer into soluble and low-molecular-weight fractions, but final <3 kDa ultrafiltrable iron did not increase proportionally with initial iron loading. The common-backbone model comparison supported an indirect contribution of metal-center occupancy to local interfacial dynamics. MD simulations further suggested greater interface expansion and rearrangement in AB at 57.5 °C, whereas HB exhibited more constrained relative motion. These results indicate that LF iron saturation regulates thermal aggregation and iron partitioning during digestion through modulation of LF conformation and interfacial dynamics.
